28 JANUARY 2003. — Act on the allocation of the family home to the spouse or legal cohabitant victim of acts of physical violence by his or her partner, and supplementing article 410 of the Criminal Code (1)

ALBERT II, King of the Belgians,
To all, present and to come, Greetings.  
The Houses have adopted and We sanction the following:
Article 1. This Act regulates a matter referred to in article 78 of the Constitution.

### Art. 2. Article 410, paragraph 2, of the Criminal Code, inserted by the Act of

24 November 1997 and amended by the Act of 28 November 2000, is supplemented as follows:
"Furthermore, in the case referred to in article 398, paragraph 1, the maximum penalty is increased to one year's imprisonment."

### Art. 3

In article 223 of the Civil Code, the following paragraph is inserted between paragraphs 2 and 3:
"If one spouse has committed against the other an act referred to in articles 375, 398 to 400, 402, 403 or 405 of the Criminal Code or has attempted to commit an act referred to in articles 375, 393, 394 or 397 of the same Code, or if there are serious indications of such behaviour, the victim spouse shall be granted, except in exceptional circumstances, the use of the matrimonial home if he or she so requests."

28 JANUARI 2003. — Wet tot toewijzing van de gezinswoning aan de echtgenoot of aan de wettelijk samenwonende die het slachtoffer is van fysieke gewelddaden vanwege zijn partner en tot aanvulling van artikel 410 van het Strafwetboek (1)

ALBERT II, Koning der Belgen,
Aan allen die nu zijn en hierna wezen zullen, Onze Groet.  
De Kamers hebben aangenomen en Wij bekrachtigen hetgeen volgt:

### Artikel 1

Deze wet regelt een aangelegenheid als bedoeld in artikel 78 van de Grondwet.

### Art. 2

Artikel 410, tweede lid, van het Strafwetboek, ingevoegd bij de wet van 24 november 1997 en gewijzigd bij de wet van 28 novem-ber 2000, wordt aangevuld als volgt:
« Bovendien wordt de maximumstraf, in het geval bepaald in artikel 398, eerste lid, verhoogd tot gevangenisstraf van een jaar. »

### Art. 3

In artikel 223 van het Burgerlijk Wetboek wordt tussen het tweede en het derde lid het volgende lid ingevoegd:
« Indien een echtgenoot zich tegenover de andere schuldig gemaakt heeft aan een feit als bedoeld in de artikelen 375, 398 tot 400, 402, 403 of
405 van het Strafwetboek, of heeft gepoogd een feit te plegen als bedoeld in de artikelen 375, 393, 394 of 397 van hetzelfde Wetboek, of indien er ernstige aanwijzingen voor dergelijke gedragingen bestaan, zal de echtgenoot die het slachtoffer is, behalve bij uitzonderlijke omstandigheden, het genot toegewezen krijgen van de echtelijke verblijfplaats indien hij daarom verzoekt. »

### Art. 4

In artikel 1447 van hetzelfde Wetboek, ingevoegd bij de wet van 14 juli 1976, wordt tussen het eerste en het tweede lid het volgende lid ingevoegd:
« Behoudens uitzonderlijke omstandigheden wordt het verzoek ingewilligd dat uitgaat van de echtgenoot die slachtoffer is van een feit als bedoeld in de artikelen 375, 398 tot 400, 402, 403 of 405 van het Strafwetboek of van een poging tot een feit als bedoeld in de artikelen 375, 393, 394 of 397 van hetzelfde Wetboek, hetzij wanneer de andere echtgenoot uit dien hoofde is veroordeeld bij een in kracht van gewijsde gegane beslissing, hetzij wanneer de beslissing die de echtscheiding uitspreekt geheel of gedeeltelijk op dat feit is gegrond. »

### Art. 5

Artikel 1479 van hetzelfde Wetboek, ingevoegd bij de wet van 23 november 1998, wordt aangevuld met het volgende lid:
« Indien een wettelijk samenwonende zich tegenover de andere schuldig gemaakt heeft aan een feit als bedoeld in de artikelen 375, 398 tot 400, 402, 403 of 405 van het Strafwetboek, of heeft gepoogd een feit te plegen als bedoeld in de artikelen 375, 393, 394 of 397 van hetzelfde Wetboek, of indien er ernstige aanwijzingen voor dergelijke gedragin-gen bestaan, zal deze laatste behalve bij uitzonderlijke omstandigheden het genot van de gemeenschappelijke verblijfplaats toegewezen krijgen indien hij daarom verzoekt. »

In article 1447 of the same Code, inserted by the law of 14 July 1976, the following paragraph is inserted between paragraphs 1 and 2:

"The request made by the spouse who has been the victim of an act referred to in articles 375, 398 to 400, 402, 403 or 405 of the Criminal Code or of an attempt to commit an act referred to in articles 375, 393, 394 or 397 of the same Code shall be granted, except in exceptional circumstances, either when the other spouse has been convicted on that ground by a decision that has acquired the force of res judicata and the divorce has been pronounced against him or her, or when the decision pronouncing the divorce is based wholly or partly on that act."

### Art. 5

Article 1479 of the same Code, inserted by the law of 23 November 1998, is supplemented by the following paragraph:
"If a legal cohabitant has committed against the other an act referred to in articles 375, 398 to 400, 402, 403 or 405 of the Criminal Code or has attempted to commit an act referred to in articles 375, 393, 394 or 397 of the same Code, or if there are serious indications of such behaviour, the latter shall be granted, except in exceptional circumstances, the enjoyment of the common residence if he or she so requests."

## CHAPTER IV

Amendment of the law of 13 May 1999 containing the disciplinary statute of members of the police services

### Art. 10

Article 26 of the law of 13 May 1999 on the disciplinary statute of members of the personnel of the police services is supplemented by the following paragraphs:
"When the Centre for Equal Opportunities and Opposition to Racism communicates to the Standing Committee for the Supervision of the Police Services or to the General Inspectorate of the Federal Police and the Local Police facts suggesting discriminatory treatment within the meaning of the law of 30 July 1981 to suppress certain acts inspired by racism or xenophobia or of the law of 6 January 2003 to combat discrimination and amending the law of 15 February 1993 establishing a Centre for Equal Opportunities and Opposition to Racism, the chairman of the Standing Committee or the Inspector General, as the case may be, shall have an investigation conducted into these facts, inform the competent authority and refer the matter to the disciplinary or judicial authority if the facts so justify. The chairman of the Standing Committee or the Inspector General, as the case may be, shall inform the Centre of the follow-up given to its actions and in particular of the action taken by the disciplinary or judicial authority in examining the facts.  

If the Standing Committee or the General Inspectorate is seized of facts suggesting discriminatory treatment within the meaning of the aforementioned laws, the chairman of the Standing Committee or the Inspector General, as the case may be, shall inform the Centre for Equal Opportunities and Opposition to Racism without communicating the identity of the parties concerned. He shall also inform it of the action taken by the disciplinary or judicial authority in examining the facts."

### Art. 3

The practical aptitude examination consists of a written and an oral test, which are equivalent, dealing directly or indirectly with the following subjects:
1˚ general accounting;  
2˚ legislation on accounting and the annual accounts of enterprises;  
3˚ general principles of financial management;  
4˚ the preparation, analysis and critical assessment of annual accounts;  
5˚ organisation of accounting services and administrative services of the enterprise;  
6˚ value added tax; 7˚ personal income tax;  
8˚ corporate income tax; 9˚ tax procedures;  
10˚ company law and legislation relating to enterprises in difficulties;  
11˚ principles of registration and succession duties;  
12˚ principles relating to customs and excise duties;  
13˚ principles of labour law and social security;  
14˚ professional ethics of certified accountants and certified accountants-tax advisers.

### Art. 4

§ 1. The written test of the aptitude examination for access to the title of certified accountant or certified accountant-tax adviser concerns the resolution of one or more practical cases relating to the subjects referred to in Article 3.

### § 2

During the written test of the aptitude examination for access to the title of certified accountant-tax adviser, a more thorough knowledge of the subjects referred to in Article 3, 6˚, 7˚, 8˚, 9˚, 11˚ and 12˚ shall be required.

### Art. 5

The oral test comprises a commentary on the written test and an examination on the practice of the function, the tasks, the liability and the professional ethics of certified accountants and certified accountants-tax advisers.  
Only candidates who have obtained at least fifty per cent of the points after the written test are admitted to the oral test.  
Candidates for the title of certified accountant-tax adviser must in addition have obtained at least sixty per cent of the points in the written test concerning the subjects mentioned in Article 4, § 2, in order to be admitted to the oral test.

## CHAPTER III

Conditions relating to admission to and organisation of the practical aptitude examination

### Art. 6

The candidate who wishes to participate in the practical aptitude examination shall address a written request to the Traineeship Commission, referred to in Chapter IV.

### Art. 7

The candidate is admitted to the practical aptitude examination as soon as he has completed his traineeship in accordance with the legal and regulatory provisions as well as the guidelines issued by the Council, which must be complied with by the trainee accountant or trainee accountant-tax adviser during his traineeship.  
The Institute shall notify in writing within a period of one month the trainee who has submitted a written request, as referred to in Article 6, of the date of the next practical aptitude examination. If the trainee does not satisfy the conditions for participating in the practical aptitude examination, he shall be informed thereof in writing. He may submit a new request, in accordance with Article 6, as soon as he satisfies the conditions of access referred to in the first paragraph.

### Art. 8

The practical aptitude examination is organised at least twice a year by the Institute and may be taken in one of the three national languages at the candidate's choice.

### Art. 9

The results are notified by the Institute to the candidate within three months of the practical aptitude examination and are added to his file.

### Art. 10

Candidates who, after the oral part, have obtained sixty per cent of the points, have passed and are considered to have submitted an application for registration in the register of holders of the profession referred to in Article 46 of the Royal Decree of 27 November 1985 determining the rules of organisation and functioning of the professional institutes created for the intellectual professions providing services. The list of candidates who have passed is transmitted to the Chamber which shall proceed with their registration in the register of holders of the profession, in accordance with Article 8, § 1, 1˚, of the framework law.

### Art. 11

If the candidate has not passed in accordance with Article 10, he may submit in writing a new request, in accordance with Article 6, with a view to being admitted to the following practical aptitude examination, until the expiry of the maximum traineeship period of 36 months referred to in Article 51 of the law.

## CHAPTER IV. — The Traineeship Commission/The examination board

### Art. 12

A Traineeship Commission is established within the Institute. This Traineeship Commission acts as an examination board, as referred to in Article 51 of the law and is responsible for conducting the practical aptitude examination organised by the Institute.

### Art. 13

In the exercise of its mission, the Traineeship Commission has the most extensive powers of supervision and control. It may delegate to one or more of its members the tasks entrusted to it.

### Art. 10

Candidates who, after the oral part, have obtained sixty percent of the points to be achieved, have passed and are deemed to have made their application for registration on the tableau as referred to in Article 46 of the Royal Decree of 27 November 1985 determining the rules concerning the organisation and functioning of the professional institutes established for the intellectual service professions. If the candidate has not passed in accordance with Article 10, he may submit a new application in accordance with Article 6 to be admitted to the next practical aptitude examination, and this until the expiry of the maximum traineeship period of 36 months as provided for in Article 51 of the law.

## CHAPTER IV. — The Traineeship Commission/Examination Jury

### Art. 12

A Traineeship Commission is established within the Institute. This Traineeship Commission acts as examination jury, as referred to in Article 51 of the law, and is responsible for conducting the practical aptitude examination organised by the Institute.

### Art. 13

The Traineeship Commission has, in the exercise of its mandate, the broadest means of supervision and control. It may entrust the tasks assigned to it to one or more of its members.

### Art. 14

§ 1. The Traineeship Commission has twenty effective members, including the president and vice-president of the Institute. Ten members are French-speaking and ten members are Dutch-speaking. The effective members are, on proposal of the Bureau, designated by the Council for a renewable term of four years. This designation takes place at the second meeting following the elections of the newly constituted Council. The appointments of the members of the Traineeship Commission are subject to the approval of the Minister who has the Middle Classes in his attributions.

### § 2

The president and vice-president of the Institute are also president and vice-president of the Traineeship Commission.

### § 3

Where appropriate, the Council may, on proposal of the Bureau, appoint alternate members whose mandate expires at the same time as that of the effective members elected in accordance with § 1. The alternate members may only attend meetings of the Traineeship Commission when they are convened to replace an effective member.

### Art. 15

§ 1. There is incompatibility between the mandate of member of the Traineeship Commission and the mandate of:
1° Effective or alternate member of the Chamber;  
2° Effective or alternate member of the Appeal Chamber.

### § 2

The president and vice-president excepted, the Traineeship Commission may include at most five Dutch-speaking members and five French-speaking members who are also members of the Council.

### § 3

At least one French-speaking member and one Dutch-speaking member must be professors or lecturers at a university, at an institution of higher education of university level or at an institution of higher economic education.

### § 4

One of the members of the Traineeship Commission must possess sufficient knowledge of the German language.

### § 5

The other members of the Traineeship Commission must be members of the Institute or persons chosen on the basis of their specific knowledge of matters relevant to the profession.

### Art. 16

§ 1. The Traineeship Commission meets on convocation of its president or, in case of absence, of its vice-president. The member who is prevented gives timely notice to the president.

### § 2

The meetings of the Traineeship Commission are chaired by the president or, in his absence, by the vice-president. If both are absent, the session is chaired by the oldest member. The acting president has the same prerogatives as the president.

### § 3

The Traineeship Commission deliberates by linguistic role. It can only validly deliberate when at least six members of each linguistic role are present. Decisions are taken by simple majority of votes. In case of a tie, the vote of the president is decisive.

## CHAPTER V. — Exemptions

### Art. 17

§ 1. Certified accountants, members of the Professional Institute of Certified Accountants and Tax Advisers, who hold a diploma allowing access to the title of certified accountant-tax adviser, and who apply for their registration on the tableau of certified accountants-tax advisers, are exempted from the completion of the traineeship. ### § 2

It is the Traineeship Commission that will be responsible for conducting the practical aptitude examination referred to in § 1, which will consist of an oral test.

### Artikel 1

bepaalt dat een ontvangstmelding wordt uitgereikt teneinde aan de aanvrager te bevestigen dat zijn aanvraag werd ontvangen. Deze uitreiking dient te gebeuren binnen de vijf werkdagen vanaf de datum van ontvangst van de aanvraag.  
Deze formaliteit moet duidelijk worden onderscheiden van deze welke is voorzien in artikel 21, 6e lid, van de voormelde wet van 24 december 2002, die ertoe strekt de aanvrager in kennis te stellen van de uiterste datum waarop een beslissing van de administratie moet totstandkomen, van zodra deze laatste vaststelt dat de ingediende aanvraag volledig is. Welnu, deze vaststelling vereist een eerste onderzoek nopens de grond van de aanvraag en in voorkomend geval zal de aanvrager verzocht worden deze te vervolledigen.

### Artikel 2

voorziet in de mogelijkheid om eender welke ambtenaar van de FOD Financie¨n te betrekken bij het onderzoek van de aanvragen. Deze raadpleging kan, voor zover dat nodig mocht zijn, op collegiale wijze worden georganiseerd en dit via oprichting van kennisgroepen. Deze groepen van ambtenaren zullen de kennis die noodzakelijk is bij de behandeling van bepaalde materies kunnen aanleveren. Er zal niet systematisch een beroep worden gedaan op een dergelijke groep, maar enkel wanneer zulks nuttig blijkt te zijn, inzonderheid bij de behandeling van aanvragen die slaan op verschil-lende belastingen, voor complexe aanvragen die een gezamenlijke inzet vergen van technische of juridische expertise van verschillende dien-sten of nog, indien mocht blijken dat een aanvraag een nieuw standpunt noodzaakt betreffende de toepassing van een bestaande wettelijke bepaling.  

En réponse à la remarque du Conseil d’Etat concernant cette disposition, il est précisé que la participation de tout fonctionnaire du SPF Finances dont la collaboration s’avèrera utile pour l’instruction de la demande, comme indiqué à l’alinéa précédent, est prévue de manière expresse dans le présent arrêté afin de prévenir toute contestation éventuelle, fondée sur d’autres dispositions réglementaires, concernant la validité de décisions marquées par une telle collaboration. En effet, le service des décisions anticipées auprès duquel les demandes devront être introduites n’est pas appelé à instruire ces demandes de manière exclusive en toutes circonstances. En outre, une disposition visant un objectif semblable de sécurité juridique dans le cadre d’une assistance à la décision était déjà prévue par l’arrêté royal du 4 avril 1995 relatif à la Commission des accords fiscaux préalables, confirmé par la loi du 2 juin 1998.  

Le projet soumis à l’avis du Conseil d’Etat prévoyait que: « Tout service concerné par la demande doit être consulté lors du traitement de celle-ci. » Cette disposition a été retirée de l’arrêté compte tenu de l’avis du Conseil d’Etat. Cela étant, on veillera pour la bonne application du nouveau système à ce que les services concernés par la demande soient consultés suivant des modalités appropriées et conci-liables avec les objectifs poursuivis par l’adoption du nouveau système de décision anticipée.  

Il va de soi que conforme´ment au droit commun, le demandeur pourra se faire assister ou repre´senter a` tous les stades de la proce´dure.  

L’article 2 prévoit en outre que le demandeur pourra demander à rencontrer les fonctionnaires chargés de l’instruction de sa demande pour leur présenter son argumentation et entendre leurs éventuelles remarques, questions et réserves.  

Il a été spécifié dans l’exposé des motifs de la loi précitée que la demande de décision anticipée est une possibilité offerte aux contri-buables et en aucun cas une obligation. Dans cet esprit, le demandeur peut retirer sa demande à tout moment de la procédure, sans que cette précision doive être prévue par voie réglementaire. L’arrêté a donc été adapté en ce sens conformément à l’ avis du Conseil d’Etat.  

L’article 3 pre´voit une de´le´gation au Ministre des Finances ou a` son de´le´gue´ afin de de´signer les fonctionnaires charge´s de se prononcer sur les demandes.  

Conforme´ment a` l’obligation de motivation des actes administratifs, la de´cision anticipe´e – favorable ou de´favorable — devra eˆtre claire-ment justifie´e eu e´gard notamment aux arguments avance´s par le demandeur tout au long de la proce´dure.  

L’article 4 pre´voit que la de´cision est notifie´e au demandeur par pli recommande´ a` la poste afin de s’assurer de sa bonne re´ception par l’inte´resse´.  

L’article 24 de la loi pre´cite´e pre´voit la publication des de´cisions anticipe´es de manie`re rapide et anonyme, dans le respect du secret professionnel. L’article 5 du pre´sent arreˆte´ pre´voit que les de´cisions anticipe´es seront publie´es sous la forme de synthe`se individuelle ou collective. Cette publication pourra notamment se faire, dans la mesure du possible, sur le site internet du SPF Finances.  

A cet e´gard, la de´cision anticipe´e pouvant reveˆtir un caracte`re international ou` un contribuable e´tranger et une administration fiscale e´trange`re pourraient eˆtre parties a` la de´cision, il conviendra de tenir compte de l’avis de toutes ces parties quant a` la publicite´ a` donner ou non a` la de´cision.  

En outre, la notion de secret professionnel doit eˆtre comprise au sens large, et prendre en compte e´galement le respect de la confidentialite´ des affaires du demandeur qui pourra, pour de justes motifs, revendi-quer l’absence ou le report de publication de la de´cision qui le concerne.  

In antwoord op de opmerking van de Raad van State met betrekking tot deze bepaling, wordt verduidelijkt dat de deelname van elke ambtenaar van de FOD Financiën waarvan de medewerking, zoals aangegeven in de vorige alinea, nuttig zou zijn bij het onderzoek van de aanvraag, uitdrukkelijk is voorzien in dit besluit teneinde elke even-tuele, op andere reglementaire bepalingen gegronde betwisting over de geldigheid van beslissingen die blijk geven van dergelijke samenwer-king te voorkomen. De dienst van voorafgaande beslissingen bij dewelke de aanvragen zullen moeten worden ingediend is er namelijk niet toe gehouden deze aanvragen in alle omstandigheden alleen te onderzoeken. Daarenboven was in het koninklijk besluit van 4 april 1995 met betrekking tot de Commissie voor voorafgaande fiscale akkoorden, bekrachtigd door de wet van 2 juni 1998, reeds voorzien in een bepaling met een gelijkaardig oogmerk van juridische zekerheid in het kader van verlenen van bijstand bij het beslissingsproces.  

Het ontwerp dat werd onderworpen aan het advies van de Raad van State bepaalde: « Elke bij de aanvraag betrokken dienst moet bij de behandeling ervan worden geraadpleegd. » Deze bepaling werd in het besluit geschrapt rekening houdende met het advies van de Raad van State. Derhalve zal er moeten over worden gewaakt dat, voor de goede werking van het nieuwe systeem, de diensten welke de aanvraag aanbelangen, worden geraadpleegd overeenkomstig passende modali-teiten welke verenigbaar zijn met de doelstellingen die door het invoeren van het nieuwe systeem van voorafgaande beslissingen worden nagestreefd.  

Het spreekt vanzelf dat, overeenkomstig het gemeen recht, de aanvrager tijdens iedere fase van de procedure zich kan laten bijstaan of laten vertegenwoordigen.

### Artikel 1

provides that an acknowledgement of receipt shall be issued in order to confirm to the applicant that his application has been received. This issue must take place within five working days from the date of receipt of the application.  
This formality must be clearly distinguished from that provided for in Article 21, 6th paragraph, of the aforementioned Act of 24 December 2002, which aims to inform the applicant of the final date by which a decision of the administration must be made, as soon as the latter establishes that the submitted application is complete. However, this establishment requires an initial examination regarding the substance of the application and, where appropriate, the applicant will be requested to complete it.

### Artikel 2

provides for the possibility of involving any official of the FPS Finance in the examination of applications. This consultation may, insofar as necessary, be organised in a collegial manner through the establishment of knowledge groups. These groups of officials will be able to provide the knowledge necessary for the processing of certain matters. Such a group will not be systematically called upon, but only when this proves useful, in particular in the processing of applications relating to different taxes, for complex applications requiring a joint deployment of technical or legal expertise from different services or, if it appears that an application necessitates a new position regarding the application of an existing legal provision.  

In response to the remark of the Council of State concerning this provision, it is specified that the participation of any official of the FPS Finance whose collaboration proves useful for the examination of the application, as indicated in the preceding paragraph, is expressly provided for in this decree in order to prevent any possible challenge, based on other regulatory provisions, concerning the validity of decisions marked by such collaboration. Indeed, the advance decisions service with which applications must be submitted is not called upon to examine these applications exclusively in all circumstances. Moreover, a provision pursuing a similar objective of legal certainty in the context of decision-making assistance was already provided for by the Royal Decree of 4 April 1995 relating to the Commission for Advance Tax Rulings, confirmed by the Act of 2 June 1998.  

The draft submitted to the opinion of the Council of State provided that: "Any service concerned by the application must be consulted during its processing." This provision has been removed from the decree in view of the opinion of the Council of State. That being said, care will be taken for the proper application of the new system to ensure that the services concerned by the application are consulted according to appropriate procedures that are reconcilable with the objectives pursued by the adoption of the new advance decision system.  

It goes without saying that in accordance with common law, the applicant may be assisted or represented at all stages of the procedure.  

Article 2 further provides that the applicant may request to meet the officials responsible for examining his application in order to present his arguments and hear their possible remarks, questions and reservations.  

It was specified in the explanatory memorandum of the aforementioned Act that the request for an advance decision is a possibility offered to taxpayers and in no case an obligation. In this spirit, the applicant may withdraw his application at any stage of the procedure, without this specification needing to be provided by regulatory means. The decree has therefore been adapted accordingly in accordance with the opinion of the Council of State.  

Article 3 provides for a delegation to the Minister of Finance or his delegate in order to designate the officials responsible for ruling on applications.  

In accordance with the obligation to give reasons for administrative acts, the advance decision – favourable or unfavourable – must be clearly justified having regard in particular to the arguments put forward by the applicant throughout the procedure.  

Article 4 provides that the decision is notified to the applicant by registered mail in order to ensure its proper reception by the person concerned.  

Article 24 of the aforementioned Act provides for the publication of advance decisions in a rapid and anonymous manner, in compliance with professional secrecy. Article 5 of this decree provides that advance decisions will be published in the form of individual or collective summaries. This publication may in particular be made, insofar as possible, on the website of the FPS Finance.  

In this regard, as the advance decision may have an international character where a foreign taxpayer and a foreign tax administration could be parties to the decision, account should be taken of the opinion of all these parties as to whether or not to give publicity to the decision.  

Moreover, the notion of professional secrecy must be understood in a broad sense, and also take into account respect for the confidentiality of the applicant's affairs, who may, for just reasons, claim the absence or postponement of publication of the decision concerning him.  

In response to the remark of the Council of State concerning this provision, it is clarified that the participation of any official of the FPS Finance whose collaboration, as indicated in the previous paragraph, would be useful in the examination of the application, is expressly provided for in this decree in order to prevent any possible challenge, based on other regulatory provisions, concerning the validity of decisions showing such collaboration. Indeed, the advance decisions service with which applications must be submitted is not obliged to examine these applications alone in all circumstances. Moreover, a provision with a similar objective of legal certainty in the context of providing assistance in the decision-making process was already provided for in the Royal Decree of 4 April 1995 relating to the Commission for Advance Tax Rulings, confirmed by the Act of 2 June 1998.  

The draft that was submitted to the opinion of the Council of State provided: "Any service involved in the application must be consulted during its processing." This provision was deleted from the decree taking into account the opinion of the Council of State. Consequently, care must be taken to ensure that, for the proper functioning of the new system, the services concerned by the application are consulted in accordance with appropriate procedures that are compatible with the objectives pursued by the introduction of the new advance decisions system.  

It goes without saying that, in accordance with common law, the applicant may be assisted or represented during any stage of the procedure.

provides for a delegation to the Minister of Finance or his delegate to designate the officials who are responsible for ruling on the applications.

provides that the decision is notified to the applicant by registered letter sent by post in order to ensure its proper receipt by the interested party.

of the aforementioned law provides for the publication of advance decisions in a rapid and anonymous manner and with respect for professional secrecy.

of this decree provides that advance decisions will be published in the form of individual or collective summaries. This publication may, to the extent possible, take place via the website of the FPS Finance.

30 JANUARY 2003. — Royal decree taken in execution of Article 26 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the regime of companies in matters of income taxes and establishing a system of advance decision in tax matters (1)
ALBERT II, King of the Belgians,
To all, present and to come, Greetings.
Having regard to Article 26 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the regime of companies in matters of income taxes and establishing a system of advance decision in tax matters;
Having regard to the opinion of the Inspector of Finance, given on 5 December 2002; Having regard to the agreement of the Minister of Budget, given on 5 December 2002;
Having regard to the urgency motivated by the fact:
—	that the provisions of this decree are taken in application of Article 26 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the regime of companies in matters of income taxes and establishing a system of advance decision in tax matters;
—	that the provisions of Articles 20 to 28 of the same law apply from 1 January 2003;
—	that it is therefore appropriate to bring the provisions of this decree into force from the same date in order to ensure the immediate functioning of the system of advance decision in tax matters;
Having regard to the opinion of the Council of State, given on 15 January 2003 in application of Article 84, paragraph 1, 2°, of the coordinated laws on the Council of State;
On the proposal of Our Minister of Finance and on the opinion of Our Ministers who deliberated thereon in Council,
We have decreed and decree:
Article 1. Requests for advance decisions referred to in Article 20 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the regime of companies in matters of income taxes and establishing a system of advance decision in tax matters are the subject of an acknowledgement of receipt issued to the applicant within a period of five working days from the date of receipt of the request.

### Artikel 6

sets the final date for submission to the Minister of Finance of the annual activity report at 30 June of the year following the reference year.

### Artikel 7

contains the repeal provisions of the regulatory provisions that were applicable to the old "ruling" practice.

30 JANUARY 2003. — Royal decree implementing Article 26 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the corporate regime with regard to income taxes and establishing a system of advance decisions in tax matters (1)
ALBERT II, King of the Belgians,
To all those who are now and will be hereafter, Our Greeting.  
Having regard to Article 26 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the corporate regime with regard to income taxes and establishing a system of advance decisions in tax matters;  
Having regard to the opinion of the Inspector of Finance given on 5 December 2002;  
Having regard to the agreement of the Minister of Budget of 5 December 2002;  
Having regard to the urgent necessity motivated by the fact:
—	that the provisions of this decree are adopted in implementation of Article 26 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the corporate regime with regard to income taxes and establishing a system of advance decisions in tax matters;  
—	that the provisions of Articles 20 to 28 of the same law take effect from 1 January 2003;  
—	that it is therefore appropriate to bring the provisions of this decree into force on the same date in order to ensure the operation of the system of advance decisions in tax matters immediately;  
Having regard to the opinion of the Council of State given on 15 January 2003 in application of Article 84, first paragraph, 2°, of the coordinated laws on the Council of State;  
On the proposal of Our Minister of Finance, and on the advice of Our Ministers assembled in Council,
We have decreed and decree:

### Article 1

The applications for advance decisions referred to in Article 20 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the corporate regime with regard to income taxes and establishing a system of advance decisions in tax matters shall be the subject of an acknowledgement of receipt issued to the applicant within a period of five working days from the date of receipt of the application.

### Art. 2

Any official of the Federal Public Service Finance may take part in the examination of the application.  

The applicant may be heard on his own initiative or at his request.

### Art. 3

The Minister of Finance or his delegate designates the officials of the Federal Public Service Finance responsible for ruling on applications for advance decisions.

### Art. 4

The decision is notified to the applicant by registered mail.

### Art. 5

Advance decisions are published in the form of individual or collective summaries.

### Art. 6

The annual report referred to in Article 25 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the corporate regime with regard to income taxes and establishing a system of advance decisions in tax matters shall be sent to the Minister of Finance no later than 30 June of the year following that to which the report relates.

### Art. 7

The royal decree of 4 April 1995 relating to the Commission for Advance Tax Agreements, confirmed by the law of 2 June 1998, the royal decree of 3 May 1999 organising a system of advance decisions in tax matters, the ministerial decree of 27 May 1999 granting delegation to rule on applications for advance decisions in tax matters and the ministerial decree of 6 June 2000 appointing the members of the Commission for Advance Tax Agreements, amended by the ministerial decree of 4 January 2002, are repealed.

### Art. 8

§ 1. The royal decree of 4 April 1995 relating to the Commission for Advance Tax Agreements, confirmed by the law of 2 June 1998, and the ministerial decree of 6 June 2000 appointing the members of the Commission for Advance Tax Agreements, amended by the ministerial decree of 4 January 2002, as they existed before being repealed by Article 7, continue to apply to applications for advance tax agreements submitted before the date of entry into force of this decree in accordance with Article 18, § 3 to § 6, of the Code of Registration, Mortgage and Clerk's Fees, and Article 345 of the Income Tax Code 1992, as they existed before their repeal by Article 27 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the corporate regime with regard to income taxes and establishing a system of advance decisions in tax matters, and Article 106, paragraph 2, of the Succession Duties Code, as it existed before being replaced by Article 28 of the same law.  

The royal decree of 3 May 1999 organising a system of advance decisions in tax matters and the ministerial decree of 27 May 1999 granting delegation to rule on applications for advance decisions in tax matters, as they existed before being repealed by Article 7, continue to apply to applications for advance decisions submitted before the date of entry into force of this decree.

### § 2

The advance decisions service established by Article 2 of the aforementioned royal decree of 3 May 1999 as it existed before being repealed by Article 7 continues to carry out its tasks until the decisions relating to the applications referred to in § 1, paragraphs 1 and 2, have been published and the reports relating to those activities have been submitted to the competent authority.

### Art. 2

Any official of the Federal Public Service Finance may participate in the examination of the application.  

The applicant may be heard, whether or not at his request.

### Art. 3

The Minister of Finance or his delegate designates the officials of the Federal Public Service Finance who are responsible for ruling on applications for advance decisions.

### Art. 4

The decision is brought to the knowledge of the applicant by registered letter.

### Art. 5

Advance decisions are published in the form of individual or collective summaries.

### Art. 6

The annual report referred to in Article 25 of the law of 24 December 2002 amending the corporate regime with regard to income taxes and establishing a system of advance decisions in tax matters shall be sent to the Minister of Finance no later than 30 June of the year following that to which the report relates.

### Art. 7

The royal decree of 4 April 1995 relating to the Commission for Advance Tax Agreements, confirmed by the law of 2 June 1998, the royal decree of 3 May 1999 organising a system of advance decisions in tax matters, the ministerial decree of 27 May 1999 granting delegation to decide on applications for advance decisions in tax matters and the ministerial decree of 6 June 2000 appointing the members of the Commission for Advance Tax Agreements, amended by ministerial decree of 4 January 2002, are repealed.

Having regard to the royal decree of 29 June 1973 establishing the remuneration regulations for staff of the federal public services, in particular Article 14, § 1, second paragraph, inserted by the royal decree of 27 March 2001 and amended by the royal decree of 5 September 2002;
Having regard to the royal decree of 8 August 1983 concerning the exercise of a higher office in the State administrations, in particular Article 7, § 3, amended by the royal decree of 20 February 1989;
Having regard to the royal decree of 3 September 2000 regulating the contribution of the State and certain public institutions to the transport costs of federal staff members and amending the royal decree of 20 April 1999 granting an allowance for the use of bicycles to staff members of certain federal public services, in particular Articles 6, 9 and 10;
Having regard to the opinion of the Inspector of Finance, given on 19 August 2002;
Having regard to the agreement of Our Minister of Budget of 29 August 2002;
Having regard to protocol No. 435 of 17 September 2002 of the Committee of the federal community and regional public services;
Having regard to protocol N-156 of 18 October 2002 of the Negotiating Committee of the military personnel of the armed forces;
Having regard to the decision of the Council of Ministers on the request to the Council of State to give an opinion within a period of one month;
Having regard to opinion 34.443/1 of the Council of State given on 12 December 2002, in application of Article 84, first paragraph, 1° of the coordinated laws on the Council of State;
On the proposal of Our Minister of the Civil Service and Modernisation of Public Administrations and on the opinion of Our Ministers assembled in Council,
We have decreed and decree:

### Article 1

In Article 3, second paragraph, of the royal decree of 12 May 1927 concerning the retirement age of civil servants, officials and service staff of the State, replaced by the royal decree of 13 September 1989, the words "and subject to the agreement of the Minister responsible for the Civil Service" are deleted.

### Art. 2

Article 14, § 1, second paragraph, of the royal decree of 29 June 1973 establishing the remuneration regulations for staff of the federal public services, inserted by the royal decree of 27 March 2001, and amended by the royal decree of 5 September 2002, is repealed.

### Art. 3

In Article 7, § 3, of the royal decree of 8 August 1983 concerning the exercise of a higher function in the State administrations, amended by the royal decree of 20 February 1989, the following amendments are made:
1° in paragraph 5, littera b), the words "the agreement of the Minister responsible for the civil service," are deleted;
2° paragraphs 6 and 7 are repealed.

### Art. 4

In Article 6 of the royal decree of 3 September 2000 regulating the contribution of the State and certain public institutions to the transport costs of federal staff members and amending the royal decree of 20 April 1999 granting an allowance for the use of bicycles to staff members of certain federal public services, the words "or as a complete network subscription" are inserted between the words "as an urban subscription to a network" and the words ", whatever the distance".

### Art. 5. Article 9 of the same decree is replaced by the following provision

"Art. 9. - The staff member who does not use public transport daily receives a contribution of 80% towards the price of travel cards, on condition that the amount of this contribution is monthly less than that which would result from the use of a subscription and that the transport ticket is used exclusively for the journey from home to the place of work."

### Art. 6

In Article 10 of the same decree, the words "In application of Article 9 and" are deleted.

### Art. 7

This decree enters into force on the first day of the month following that in which it is published in the Belgian Official Gazette.

### Art. 8

Our Ministers and Our Secretaries of State are charged, each insofar as it concerns them, with the execution of this decree.
Given at Brussels, 3 February 2003.
ALBERT

J. VANDE LANOTTE
The Minister of the Civil Service
and Modernisation of the Administration,
L. VAN DEN BOSSCHE

Les substances interdites appartenant a` la classe (C) comprennent les exemples suivants:
1.	 Ste´ro¨ıdes anabolisants androge`nes
a/ closte´bol, fluoxymeste´rone, me´tandie´none, me´te´nolone, nandrolone, 19-norandroste´ne´diol, 19-norandroste`nedione, oxandrolone, stanozolol,

Si les tests pre´ce´dents ne sont pas disponibles, le sportif devra subir un controˆle sans annonce pre´alable au moins une fois par mois durant trois mois. Les re´sultats de ces examens devront eˆtre inclus dans le rapport. A de´faut de collaboration de la part du sportif, il en re´sultera une de´claration d’e´chantillon positif.

2.	 Autres agents anabolisants clenbute´rol, salbutamol*

* Pour le salbutamol, une concentration urinaire de salbutamol non sulfate´ supe´rieure a` 1000 nanogrammes par millilitre sera conside´re´e comme un re´sultat positif.

Les substances interdites appartenant a` la classe (D) comprennent les exemples suivants:

Les substances interdites appartenant a` la classe (E) comprennent les substances suivantes et leurs analogues ainsi que les substances mime´tiques:
1.	Gonadotrophine chorionique (hCG) chez les hommes uniquement.

Les substances interdites de la classe (G) comprennent les exemples suivants:

Les me´thodes suivantes sont interdites:  
A.	Augmentation du transfert d’oxyge`ne
Dopage sanguin: c’est l’administration de sang autologue, homologue ou he´te´rologue, ou de produits a` base de globules rouges, autrement qu’a` des fins the´rapeutiques le´gitimes.

a)	la bupivaca¨ıne, la lidoca¨ıne, la me´pivaca¨ıne, la proca¨ıne et les substances apparente´es peuvent eˆtre utilise´es mais pas la coca¨ıne; des agents vasoconstricteurs pourront eˆtre utilise´s en conjonction avec des anesthe´siques locaux;  
b)	seules des injections locales ou intra-articulaires pourront eˆtre pratique´es;

Lorsque le re`glement d’une autorite´ sportive compe´tente le pre´voit, il pourra s’ave´rer ne´cessaire de notifier l’administration des anesthe´siques locaux.

L’utilisation syste´mique des glucocorticoste´ro¨ıdes est interdite lorsque ces derniers sont administre´s par voie orale ou rectale ou par injection intraveineuse ou intramusculaire.  
Dans le cas d’une ne´cessite´ me´dicale, les injections locales et intra-articulaires de glucocorticosteroides sont autorise´es. Lorsque le re`glement d’une autorite´ sportive compe´tente le pre´voit, il pourra s’ave´rer ne´cessaire de notifier l’administration des glucocorticoste´roides.  
E.	Beˆta-bloquants

Lorsque le re`glement d’une autorite´ sportive compe´tente le pre´voit, des tests seront effectue´s pour les beˆta-bloquants.

### Art. 2

This decree enters into force on 1 January 2003. Brussels, 5 December 2002.  
For the Government of the French Community,
The Minister for Youth Assistance and Health, Mrs N. MARECHAL

Annex to the decree of 10 October 2002 relating to the procedure for controlling the practice of doping, and establishing the entry into force of the decree of 8 March 2001 relating to the promotion of health in the practice of sport, the prohibition of doping and its prevention in the French Community, amended by the decree of 5 December 2002
List of prohibited substances and methods
I. CLASSES OF PROHIBITED SUBSTANCES
A. Stimulants
a. The prohibited substances belonging to class (A. a.) include the following examples, as well as their L and D isomers:
amiphenazole, amphetamines, bromantan, caffeine*, carphedon, cocaine, ephedrines**, fencamfamine, mesocarb, pentetrazol, pipradol,
... and related substances.  
* For caffeine, a concentration in urine exceeding 12 micrograms per millilitre shall be considered a positive result.  
** For ephedrine and methylephedrine, a concentration in urine exceeding 10 micrograms per millilitre shall be considered a positive result.  
For cathine, a concentration in urine exceeding 5 micrograms per millilitre shall be considered a positive result.  
For phenylpropanolamine and pseudoephedrine, a concentration in urine exceeding 25 micrograms per millilitre shall be considered a positive result.  
NOTE: All imidazole preparations are acceptable for local application. Vasoconstrictors may be administered with local anaesthetic agents. Preparations for local use (for example nasal, ophthalmological, rectal) of adrenaline are permitted. Bupropion, synephrine and phenylephrine are permitted.  
b. The prohibited substances belonging to class (A. b.) include the following examples as well as their L and D isomers:
Formoterol***, salbutamol***, salmeterol*** and terbutaline***
... and related substances
*** Substance permitted by inhalation only to prevent and/or treat asthma and exercise-induced asthma, provided that this authorisation is prior, and issued by the competent medical authority, in application of the regulations of the sports federation or the international sports federation.  
B. Narcotics
The prohibited substances belonging to class (B) include the following examples:
buprenorphine, dextromoramide, diamorphine (heroin), methadone, morphine, pentazocine, pethidine,... and related substances.  
NOTE: Codeine, dextromethorphan, dextropropoxyphene, dihydrocodeine, diphenoxylate, ethylmorphine, pholcodine, propoxyphene and tramadol are permitted.  
C. Anabolic agents
The prohibited substances belonging to class (C) include the following examples:
1. Androgenic anabolic steroids
a/ clostebol, fluoxymesterone, metandienone, metenolone, nandrolone, 19-norandrostenediol, 19-norandrostenedione, oxandrolone, stanozolol,
... and related substances.  
b/ androstenediol, androstenedione, dehydroepiandrosterone (DHEA), dihydrotestosterone, testosterone*,
... and related substances.  
* The presence of a testosterone (T)-epitestosterone (E) ratio exceeding six (6) in the urine of an athlete constitutes an offence unless it is established that this ratio is due to a physiological or pathological condition,  
e.g. low excretion of epitestosterone, androgenic production from a tumour or enzymatic deficiencies.  
In the case of a T/E ratio exceeding 6, the sports federation or the international sports federation may, in application of its regulations, have an examination carried out under the direction of its competent medical authority before the sample is declared positive. A full report shall be drawn up; it shall include, where appropriate, a study of previous and subsequent tests as well as the results of endocrine tests. If previous tests are not available, the athlete shall undergo unannounced testing at least once a month for three months. The results of these examinations shall be included in the report. In the absence of cooperation from the athlete, this shall result in a declaration of a positive sample.  
NOTES: Evidence obtained from metabolic profiles and/or the study of isotopic ratios may be used to draw definitive conclusions.  
2. Other anabolic agents clenbuterol, salbutamol*

* For salbutamol, a urinary concentration of non-sulfated salbutamol exceeding 1000 nanograms per millilitre shall be considered a positive result.  
D. Diuretics
The prohibited substances belonging to class (D) include the following examples:
acetazolamide, ethacrynic acid, bumetanide, chlorthalidone, furosemide, hydrochlorothiazide, mannitol*, mersalyl, spironolactone, triamterene,
... and related substances.  
* Prohibited substance if injected intravenously.  
E. Peptide hormones, mimetic substances and analogues
The prohibited substances belonging to class (E) include the following substances and their analogues as well as mimetic substances:
1. Chorionic gonadotrophin (hCG) in men only.  
2. Pituitary and synthetic gonadotrophins in men only.  
3. Corticotrophins (ACTH, tetracosactide).  
4. Growth hormone (hGH).  
5. Insulin-like growth factor (IGF-1) and all their respective releasing factors as well as their analogues.  
6. Erythropoietin (EPO).  
7. Insulin*.  
* Insulin may be permitted only to treat athletes suffering from insulin-dependent diabetes, provided that this authorisation is prior, and issued by the competent medical authority, according to the regulations of the sports federation or the international sports federation.  
NOTE: The presence in the urine of an athlete of an abnormal concentration of an endogenous hormone belonging to class (E) or its diagnostic marker(s) constitutes an offence unless it is proven that it is due to a physiological or pathological condition.  
F. Agents with anti-oestrogenic action.  
Aromatase inhibitors, clomiphene, cyclofenil, tamoxifen are prohibited in men only.  
G. Masking agents.  
The prohibited substances of class (G) include the following examples:
Diuretics, epitestosterone*, probenecid, plasma substitutes (such as hydroxyethyl starch)
Masking agents are prohibited. These are products that have the capacity to hinder the excretion of prohibited substances or to conceal their presence in urine or other samples used in doping control.  
* The presence of a concentration of epitestosterone exceeding 200 ng/mL in urine constitutes an offence unless it is established that it is due to a physiological condition. Isotope ratio mass spectrometry (IRMS) may be used to draw definitive conclusions. If the results of IRMS are not conclusive, the competent medical authority shall conduct an investigation before the sample is declared positive.  
II. PROHIBITED METHODS
The following methods are prohibited:  
A. Enhancement of oxygen transfer
Blood doping: this is the administration of autologous, homologous or heterologous blood, or red blood cell products, other than for legitimate therapeutic purposes.  
The administration of products that enhance the uptake, transport or release of oxygen, such as modified haemoglobin-based products including but not limited to bovine and cross-linked haemoglobins, microencapsulated haemoglobin-based products, perfluorocarbons and RSR 13.  
B. Pharmacological, chemical and physical manipulation
Pharmacological, chemical and physical manipulation is the use of substances and methods, masking agents (see I.G), which alter, attempt to alter or may reasonably be expected to alter the integrity and validity of urine samples used in doping controls, such as, but not limited to, catheterisation, substitution and/or alteration of urine, inhibition of renal excretion and modification of measurements carried out on testosterone and epitestosterone (see I.G).  
C. Gene doping
Gene or genetic doping is defined as the non-therapeutic use of genes, genetic elements and/or cells that have the capacity to enhance sporting performance.  
III. CLASSES OF SUBSTANCES SUBJECT TO CERTAIN RESTRICTIONS
A. Alcohol
Where the regulations of a competent sports authority (sports federation or international federation) so provide, tests shall be carried out for ethanol.  
B. Cannabinoids
Where the regulations of a competent national or international sports federation so provide, tests shall be carried out for cannabinoids (such as marijuana and hashish).  
C. Local anaesthetics
Injectable local anaesthetics are permitted under the following conditions:
a) bupivacaine, lidocaine, mepivacaine, procaine and related substances may be used but not cocaine; vasoconstrictive agents may be used in conjunction with local anaesthetics;  
b) only local or intra-articular injections may be administered;  
c) only when the administration is medically justified.  
Where the regulations of a competent sports authority so provide, it may be necessary to notify the administration of local anaesthetics.  
D. Glucocorticosteroids
The systemic use of glucocorticosteroids is prohibited when they are administered orally or rectally or by intravenous or intramuscular injection.  
In the case of medical necessity, local and intra-articular injections of glucocorticosteroids are permitted. Where the regulations of a competent sports authority so provide, it may be necessary to notify the administration of glucocorticosteroids.  
E. Beta-blockers

The prohibited substances belonging to class (E) include the following examples:
acebutolol, alprenolol, atenolol, labetalol, metoprolol, nadolol, oxprenolol, propranolol, sotalol,
... and related substances.  
Where the regulations of a competent sports authority so provide, tests shall be carried out for beta-blockers.  
IV. SUMMARY TABLE OF CONCENTRATIONS IN URINE ABOVE WHICH THERE IS AN OFFENCE.  
Caffeine > 12 micrograms/millilitre Carboxy-THC > 15 nanograms/millilitre Cathine > 5 micrograms/millilitre
Ephedrine > 10 micrograms/millilitre Epitestosterone > 200 nanograms/millilitre Methylephedrine > 10 micrograms/millilitre Morphine > 1 microgram/millilitre
19-norandrosterone > 2 nanograms/millilitre in men 19-norandrosterone > 5 nanograms/millilitre in women Phenylpropanolamine > 25 micrograms/millilitre
Pseudoephedrine > 25 micrograms/millilitre
Salbutamol (as anabolic agent) > 1000 nanograms/millilitre T/E ratio* > 6
* Mentioned in points I.C.b. and I.G.  
LIST OF EXAMPLES OF PROHIBITED SUBSTANCES
WARNING: This is not an exhaustive list of prohibited substances. Many substances that are not listed in this list are considered prohibited under the designation related substances.  
Athletes must ensure that any medicine, supplement, over-the-counter preparation or any other substance they use does not contain any prohibited substance.  
STIMULANTS:

MINISTERE DE LA REGION WALLONNE
F. 2003 — 583	[C − 2003/27104]
19 DECEMBER 2002. — Order of the Walloon Government amending the order of 6 March 1997 implementing the decree of 4 July 1996 on the integration of foreign persons or persons of foreign origin

The Walloon Government,

Having regard to the decree of 4 July 1996 on the integration of foreign persons or persons of foreign origin, the salary scales of staff;  
Having regard to the order of 6 March 1997 implementing the decree of 4 July 1996 on the integration of foreign persons or persons of foreign origin;  
Having regard to the opinion of the Finance Inspectorate; Having regard to the agreement of the Minister of Budget;  
Having regard to the collective labour agreement of 16 September 2002 defining the classification of functions and the remuneration conditions for the sectors of the Joint Committee for the socio-cultural sector dependent on the Walloon Region: training through work enterprises, socio-professional integration organisations, regional integration centres for populations of foreign origin, regional employment missions and training and/or professional rehabilitation centres approved by the Walloon Agency for the professional integration of persons with disabilities;  
Having regard to the laws on the Council of State, coordinated on 12 January 1973, in particular Article 3, § 1, amended by the laws of 4 July 1989 and 4 August 1996;  
Having regard to the urgency specially motivated by the fact that, on the one hand, the collective labour agreement of 16 September 2002 provides, in its Article 8, for its retroactivity from 1 October 2001 in accordance with the non-commercial agreement and that, on the other hand, the centres are experiencing significant cash flow difficulties;  
On the proposal of the Minister of Social Affairs and Health; After deliberation,
Orders:
Article 1. This order regulates, in application of Article 138 of the Constitution, a matter referred to in Article 128,

### § 1, thereof

### Art. 2

Article 12 of the order of the Walloon Government of 6 March 1997 implementing the decree of 4 July 1996 on the integration of foreign persons or persons of foreign origin is replaced by the following provision:
« The person responsible for day-to-day management must possess:
1° a diploma of higher education, university or non-university, long-type or short-type; 2° useful experience of at least five years and professional experience of at least three years;  
3° a supplementary diploma or certificate attesting to knowledge acquired in the management of the non-commercial sector. The Minister determines the diplomas and certificates that satisfy this requirement.  
Useful experience includes experience in the sector and experience of the profession in the field of training delivered.  
Staff expenses are only taken into account for the calculation of the subsidy if they do not exceed the salary scales relating to their function and annexed to this order.  
The salary scale taken into account from 1 October 2004 for the person responsible for day-to-day management is the scale set out in Annex 2.  

If the person responsible for day-to-day management was engaged after 1 October 2001, the scales set out in Annex 2bis must be applied for the period from 1 October 2001 to 1 October 2004.  

If the person responsible for day-to-day management was engaged before 1 October 2001, the remuneration of that person must be calculated for the period from 1 October 2001 to 1 October 2004 in accordance with the calculation grid determined by Annex 3 of the collective labour agreement defining the classification of functions and the remuneration conditions for certain sectors dependent on the Walloon Region of the Joint Committee for the socio-cultural sector:  
E.F.T.,  
O.I.S.P., CRI, MIRE,  
C.F.P. of the AWIPH signed on 16 September 2002.  

For the position of secretary, the salary scale taken into account from 1 October 2004 is set out in Annex 3 or 4 depending on whether the worker holds a diploma of upper secondary education or a diploma of lower secondary education.  

If the secretary was engaged after 1 October 2001, the scales set out in Annex 3bis or 4bis must be applied for the period from 1 October 2001 to 1 October 2004, depending on whether the worker holds a diploma of upper secondary education or a diploma of lower secondary education.  

If the secretary was engaged before 1 October 2001, the remuneration of that secretary must be calculated for the period from 1 October 2001 to 1 October 2004 in accordance with the calculation grid determined by Annex 3 of the collective labour agreement defining the classification of functions and the remuneration conditions for certain sectors dependent on the Walloon Region of the Joint Committee for the socio-cultural sector:  
E.F.T.,  
O.I.S.P., CRI, MIRE,  
C.F.P. of the AWIPH signed on 16 September 2002.  

The salary scale and the annexed scales are intended to cover the gross salary to which employer social security contributions capped at 50% of the gross salary must be added. »

### Art. 3

Article 14 of the order of the Walloon Government of 6 March 1997 implementing the decree of 4 July 1996 on the integration of foreign persons or persons of foreign origin is replaced by the following provision:

« With the exception of the subsidies referred to in Article 13, paragraph 3, the approved centre is granted, during the first quarter of the calendar year, an annual advance corresponding to 85% of the amount of subsidies granted the previous year.  

To obtain payment of this advance, the service makes the request by returning to the administration a form established by it.  

The balance is paid before 1 June of the following year, upon presentation of supporting documents for the expenses. »

### Art. 4

Annex 2 is repealed and replaced by Annexes 2, 2bis, 3, 3bis, 4 and 4bis of this order.

### Art. 5

Persons responsible for day-to-day management engaged before the date of entry into force of this order are deemed to fulfil the conditions laid down by Article 2 of this order.

### Art. 6

Subject to paragraph 2, this order enters into force on the day of its adoption by the Government. Article 2 produces its effects from 1 October 2001.

Le Gouvernement wallon approuve le règlement d’ordre intérieur du Conseil régional des services de santé mental, figurant en annexe du présent arrêté.

### Art. 3

L’arrêté du 20 février 1997 portant approbation du règlement d’ordre intérieur du Conseil régional des services de santé mental est abrogé.

### Art. 4

Le présent arrêté entre en vigueur à la date de son adoption par le Gouvernement.

J.-Cl. VAN CAUWENBERGHE

Annexe
CONSEIL REGIONAL DES SERVICES DE SANTE MENTALE
Règlement d’ordre intérieur CHAPITRE Ier. — Dispositions générales
Article 1er. L’avis demandé au Conseil par le Ministre est remis, sauf disposition contraire, dans les deux mois sauf
si le Gouvernement a fixé un autre délai.  
Sur demande motivée, le Ministre peut demander un avis urgent. Dans ce cas, il fixe un délai raisonnable.

### Art. 2

Au début de chaque année civile, le Conseil fixe le calendrier des réunions ordinaires.

## CHAPITRE II. — Des convocations

### Art. 3

Le Président convoque les membres du Conseil ainsi que les personnes qui assistent aux réunions avec voix consultative.

### Art. 4

La convocation est adressée au moins huit jours avant la réunion, aux membres et contient systématiquement un modèle de procuration.  
S’il n’a pas été expédié auparavant, le procès-verbal de la réunion précédente est joint à la convocation.  
Elle énonce l’ordre du jour de la réunion. Les convocations sont envoyées à l’adresse notifiée par les membres. Elles indiquent le lieu et l’heure de la réunion. Le délai de huit jours peut être réduit en cas d’urgence.

### Art. 5. L’ordre du jour est fixé par le bureau

A l’ouverture de la réunion, l’ordre du jour ainsi que le compte-rendu de la réunion précédente sont approuvés.  
L’ordre du jour peut être modifié ou complété.

## CHAPITRE III. — Du Conseil

### Art. 6

§ 1er. Le Conseil ne peut émettre valablement un avis ou faire un rapport qu’à la condition que la moitié des membres au moins soit présente ou représentée.  
Les membres absents peuvent se faire représenter par procuration. Chaque membre présent peut être porteur d’une seule procuration.  
Les décisions sont prises à la majorité simple. En cas de parité des voix, celle du Président est prépondérante.  
Si le quorum de présence n’est pas atteint, les membres sont convoqués une nouvelle fois, au plus tard dans la quinzaine qui suit. Pour le point réinscrit à l’ordre du jour, la majorité simple des membres présents est requise.  
Si un membre s’absente du Conseil trois fois de suite, il est interpellé par le Président qui peut, en fonction des explications données par le membre concerné, proposer sa démission au Ministre.

### § 2

Le résultat du vote est joint à l’avis; à sa demande, la minorité peut joindre à l’avis de la majorité une note précisant son point de vue.

### Art. 7

Seuls les points inscrits à l’ordre du jour joints à la convocation peuvent être valablement soumis au vote.  
Toutefois, en cas d’extrême urgence dûment motivée, un point peut être ajouté à l’ordre du jour en séance dès lors que les membres présents ont accepté de l’examiner.

### Art. 8

Aucun membre du Conseil, directement intéressé à une demande d’avis soumise au Conseil - parce que membre du pouvoir organisateur ou du personnel de l’institution demanderesse - ne peut prendre part au débat et au vote relatif à l’avis concernant cette demande.  
Au cas où la réalité d’un intérêt direct dans le chef d’un ou plusieurs membre(s) est contestée, le Conseil en délibère en présence de ce(s) membre(s.)
En cas de parité des voix, la décision appartient au Président.

### Art. 9

Si le Conseil l’estime nécessaire, il peut inviter le Service de Santé mentale dont le dossier est inscrit à l’ordre du jour en vue d’obtenir des informations supplémentaires ou complémentaires.

### Art. 10. Le Conseil peut faire appel à des experts qu’il désigne

## CHAPITRE IV. — Du bureau

### Art. 11

§ 1er. Il est constitué au sein du Conseil régional des services de santé mentale, désigné ci-après le Conseil, un bureau chargé de l’organisation et de la coordination des travaux.  
Le bureau prépare les réunions du Conseil et veille à la transmission des propositions ou avis adoptés par le Conseil.  
Le bureau peut, outre les demandes d’avis du Ministre, formuler lui-même des demandes d’avis et les soumettre au Conseil.

### § 2

Le bureau se compose du Président et des deux vice-présidents désignés par le Gouvernement wallon par arrêté du 24 octobre 2002..  
Les vice-présidents assurent, à tour de rôle, la présidence des séances en cas d’empêchement du président.

### Art. 12

Les deux représentants du Gouvernement sont invités aux réunions du bureau.

### Art. 13

Le bureau peut appeler tout ou partie des membres du Conseil pour ses travaux.

## CHAPITRE V. — Des groupes de travail

### Art. 14

Pour remplir sa mission, le Conseil peut constituer des groupes de travail soit permanents, soit temporaires à l’occasion d’un problème spécifique ou dans le cadre d’une demande d’avis formulée par le Gouvernement ou le Ministre.  
Dans le cadre de ces groupes de travail, il peut faire appel à des experts.

### Art. 15. Les membres du Conseil peuvent faire partie des groupes de travail

Les membres - extérieurs au Conseil - invités à un groupe de travail déterminé le sont en fonction de leur compétence et à titre personnel, sur proposition du président du groupe de travail et avec l’accord du bureau.  
Le bureau, après avoir pris avis du président du groupe de travail, peut être amené à limiter le nombre de membres des groupes de travail selon les matières étudiées.  
La désignation des experts fait l’objet d’une décision du Conseil.

### Art. 16

A l’exception des procès-verbaux, les documents des groupes de travail sont envoyés uniquement aux membres de ces groupes.  
Les autres membres du Conseil peuvent prendre connaissance des documents au Secrétariat sur demande.  
Le membre qui s’absente des réunions d’un groupe de travail trois fois consécutivement, est considéré comme démissionnaire.

### Art. 17

Le Secrétariat du Conseil organise pratiquement les activités des groupes de travail, dans la mesure des moyens qui lui sont affectés par le Gouvernement.

### Art. 18

Les présidents des groupes de travail permanents sont désignés par le Conseil sur proposition du bureau pour une période de trois ans renouvelable une fois.  
Ils font régulièrement rapport au Conseil de l’évolution des travaux, pour approbation.  
Le Président du Conseil peut assister de plein droit à toutes les réunions des différents groupes de travail et éventuellement les présider.

J.-Cl. VAN CAUWENBERGHE
The Minister of Social Affairs and Health, Th. DETIENNE

Annex
REGIONAL COUNCIL OF MENTAL HEALTH SERVICES
Rules of procedure CHAPTER I. — General provisions
Article 1. The opinion requested from the Council by the Minister shall be delivered, unless otherwise provided, within two months unless
the Government has set another deadline.  
Upon reasoned request, the Minister may request an urgent opinion. In that case, he shall set a reasonable deadline.

### Art. 2

At the beginning of each calendar year, the Council sets the schedule of ordinary meetings.

## CHAPTER II. — Convocations

### Art. 3

The President convenes the members of the Council as well as the persons who attend meetings with consultative vote.

### Art. 4

The convocation is sent at least eight days before the meeting to the members and systematically contains a proxy form.  
If it has not been sent previously, the minutes of the previous meeting are attached to the convocation.  
It sets out the agenda of the meeting. The convocations are sent to the address notified by the members. They indicate the place and time of the meeting. The eight-day period may be reduced in case of urgency.

### Art. 5. The agenda is set by the bureau

At the opening of the meeting, the agenda as well as the minutes of the previous meeting are approved.  
The agenda may be modified or supplemented.

## CHAPTER III. — The Council

### Art. 6

§ 1. The Council may validly issue an opinion or make a report only on condition that at least half of the members are present or represented.  
Absent members may be represented by proxy. Each member present may hold only one proxy.  
Decisions are taken by simple majority. In case of a tie, the President's vote is decisive.  
If the quorum of attendance is not reached, the members are convened again, at the latest within the fortnight following. For the item re-entered on the agenda, a simple majority of the members present is required.  
If a member is absent from the Council three times in succession, he is challenged by the President who may, depending on the explanations given by the member concerned, propose his resignation to the Minister.

### § 2

The result of the vote is attached to the opinion; upon request, the minority may attach to the majority opinion a note specifying its point of view.

### Art. 7

Only items entered on the agenda attached to the convocation may be validly submitted to a vote.  
However, in case of extreme urgency duly justified, an item may be added to the agenda during the session provided that the members present have agreed to examine it.

### Art. 8

No member of the Council directly interested in a request for an opinion submitted to the Council - because he is a member of the organizing authority or the staff of the requesting institution - may take part in the debate and vote relating to the opinion concerning that request.  
In the event that the reality of a direct interest on the part of one or more member(s) is contested, the Council deliberates in the presence of that/those member(s).
In case of a tie, the decision belongs to the President.

### Art. 9

If the Council deems it necessary, it may invite the Mental Health Service whose file is entered on the agenda in order to obtain additional or supplementary information.

### Art. 10. The Council may call upon experts whom it designates

## CHAPTER IV. — The bureau

### Art. 11

§ 1. A bureau responsible for the organization and coordination of the work is established within the Regional Council of Mental Health Services, hereinafter referred to as the Council.  
The bureau prepares the meetings of the Council and ensures the transmission of proposals or opinions adopted by the Council.  
The bureau may, in addition to requests for opinions from the Minister, itself formulate requests for opinions and submit them to the Council.

### § 2

The bureau is composed of the President and the two vice-presidents designated by the Walloon Government by decree of 24 October 2002.  
The vice-presidents ensure, in turn, the chairmanship of sessions in case of impediment of the president.

### Art. 12

The two representatives of the Government are invited to the meetings of the bureau.

### Art. 13

The bureau may call all or part of the members of the Council for its work.

## CHAPTER V. — Working groups

### Art. 14

To fulfill its mission, the Council may establish working groups either permanent or temporary on the occasion of a specific problem or in the context of a request for an opinion formulated by the Government or the Minister.  
In the context of these working groups, it may call upon experts.

### Art. 15. The members of the Council may be part of the working groups

Members - external to the Council - invited to a specific working group are so invited based on their competence and in a personal capacity, on the proposal of the president of the working group and with the agreement of the bureau.  
The bureau, after having taken the opinion of the president of the working group, may be led to limit the number of members of the working groups according to the matters studied.  
The designation of experts is the subject of a decision of the Council.

### Art. 16

With the exception of minutes, the documents of the working groups are sent only to the members of those groups.  
The other members of the Council may take cognizance of the documents at the Secretariat upon request.  
The member who is absent from the meetings of a working group three times consecutively is considered to have resigned.

### Art. 17

The Secretariat of the Council practically organizes the activities of the working groups, within the limits of the means allocated to it by the Government.

### Art. 18

The presidents of the permanent working groups are designated by the Council on the proposal of the bureau for a period of three years renewable once.  
They regularly report to the Council on the progress of the work, for approval.  
The President of the Council may attend by right all the meetings of the different working groups and possibly chair them.
