g.	 code of indication assessor or certificate for application, revision or extension
h.	result of the indication assessment for application, revision or extension: here the score of the care-dependent person must be entered for the indication assessment. If no indication assessment has taken place (a certificate is used) then this field must be filled by entering "99", and not 00. So here
"fill nines" are used instead of fill zeros. The score may be entered at the moment that the care fund becomes aware of the result of the indication assessment, so before the actual decision was taken.  
i.	 code additional investigation: here it is indicated whether an additional investigation has taken place or not.  
j.	 date of indication assessment for additional investigation: date on which the additional investigation (so actually the additional indication assessment) took place
k.	 result of the indication assessment for additional investigation: here the score of the indication assessment must be entered for additional investigation. The score may be entered at the moment that the care fund becomes aware of the result of the indication assessment. If no additional investigation takes place or the result is not yet known, then this field is filled by entering "99".  

l.	 Code decision: is a consolidation of the former fields j. "Code decision" and m. "code decision after additional investigation". (The code here is the code whether or not after additional investigation). Option 3 = additional investigation in the former field j. has been replaced by field i. "code additional investigation".  
m.	 date of the decision: date on which the decision about the application, revision or extension was taken.  
n.	 date of last change of care form: date on which the last change of the care form takes effect. If there are several changes, the last date is retained. This date is the date on which the amount of the payment effectively changes. So it is always a date of the form 01/mm/yyyy.  
o.	Code care form: in this field the last valid care form is entered. The code for the application no longer needs to be provided. It is only when the application is approved that this field must be completed. When the care form changes, this field is simply adjusted and field n. "date of last change of care form" is completed.  
p.	 code decision after inspection:  
q.	result of the indication assessment for inspection: here the score of the indication assessment for inspection must be entered. If no inspection has taken place or the result of the inspection is not yet known, then this field must be filled by entering 99, and not 00. So here "fill nines" are used instead of fill zeros. The score may be entered at the moment that the care fund becomes aware of the result of the indication assessment, this can therefore fall before the date on which the actual decision of the inspection was taken.  
r.	 date of the decision after inspection: date on which the decision after inspection was taken.  
s.	 end date for execution of coverage: this field is the consolidation of fields n. "end date for execution of coverage" and x. "end date for execution of coverage after inspection or revision" in the former B files. The last valid end date must be entered here. For residential care this date is equal to "00000000".  
t.	 code payment or recovery: with this field we can determine whether field u. "amount paid or recovered during the calendar year concerned" is a positive or negative amount.  
u.	 amount that was paid or recovered during the calendar year concerned: in this field the cumulative amount (or balance) of all payments and recoveries during the calendar year concerned is recorded.

23 DECEMBER 2002. — Ministerieel besluit houdende de bepaling van de formulieren in verband met de zorgverzekering

De Vlaamse minister van Welzijn, Gezondheid, Gelijke Kansen en Ontwikkelingssamenwerking,

Gelet op het decreet van 30 maart 1999 houdende de organisatie van de zorgverzekering, gewijzigd bij de decreten van 22 december 1999, 8 december 2000, 18 mei 2001 en 20 december 2002;  
Gelet op het besluit van de Vlaamse regering van 28 september 2001 houdende de erkenning, de registratie en de machtiging, en houdende de aansluiting, de aanvraag en de tenlasteneming in het kader van de zorgverzekering, zoals gewijzigd bij de besluiten van de Vlaamse regering van 14 december 2001, 25 oktober 2002 en 13 december 2002;  
Gelet op het besluit van de Vlaamse regering van 3 juli 2002 tot bepaling van de bevoegdheden van de leden van de Vlaamse regering,
Besluit:

### Artikel 1

In uitvoering van artikel 21, § 1, artikel 29, en artikel 34, § 1, van het besluit van de Vlaamse regering van 28 september 2001 houdende de erkenning, de registratie en de machtiging, en houdende de aansluiting, de aanvraag en de tenlasteneming in het kader van de zorgverzekering gebruikt de gebruiker of zijn vertegenwoordiger een van de volgende formulieren:
1˚ het aanvraagformulier dat als bijlage I bij dit besluit gevoegd is, voor een aanvraag voor mantel- en thuiszorg; 2˚ het aanvraagformulier dat als bijlage II bij dit besluit gevoegd is, voor een aanvraag voor residentie¨le zorg.

### Art. 2

In uitvoering van artikel 37, § 1, van hetzelfde besluit gebruikt de door de zorgkas aangewezen indicatiesteller het formulier dat als bijlage III bij dit besluit gevoegd is.

### Art. 3

Het ministerieel besluit van 1 oktober 2001 houdende de bepaling van de formulieren in verband met de zorgverzekering wordt opgeheven.

23 DECEMBER 2002. — Ministerial decree determining the forms in connection with care insurance

The Flemish Minister for Welfare, Health, Equal Opportunities and Development Cooperation,

Having regard to the decree of 30 March 1999 on the organisation of care insurance, as amended by the decrees of 22 December 1999, 8 December 2000, 18 May 2001 and 20 December 2002;  
Having regard to the decree of the Flemish Government of 28 September 2001 on recognition, registration and authorisation, and on affiliation, application and assumption of costs within the framework of care insurance, as amended by the decrees of the Flemish Government of 14 December 2001, 25 October 2002 and 13 December 2002;  
Having regard to the decree of the Flemish Government of 3 July 2002 determining the powers of the members of the Flemish Government,
Decrees:

### Article 1

In implementation of Article 21, § 1, Article 29, and Article 34, § 1, of the decree of the Flemish Government of 28 September 2001 on recognition, registration and authorisation, and on affiliation, application and assumption of costs within the framework of care insurance, the user or his representative uses one of the following forms:
1˚ the application form annexed to this decree as Annex I, for an application for home and community care; 2˚ the application form annexed to this decree as Annex II, for an application for residential care.

### Art. 2

In implementation of Article 37, § 1, of the same decree, the needs assessor designated by the care fund uses the form annexed to this decree as Annex III.

### Art. 3

The ministerial decree of 1 October 2001 determining the forms in connection with care insurance is repealed.

[2003/200086]
Bericht voorgeschreven bij artikel 74 van de bijzondere wet van 6 januari 1989 op het Arbitragehof

Bij verzoekschrift dat aan het Hof is toegezonden bij op 30 januari 2003 ter post aangetekende brief en ter griffie is ingekomen op 31 januari 2003, heeft J. Van den Driessche, wonende te 1700 Dilbeek, Baron de Vironlaan 80, bus 25, beroep tot vernietiging en een vordering tot schorsing ingesteld van artikel 5 van de wet van 13 december 2002 tot wijziging van het Kieswetboek evenals zijn bijlage, en artikel 16 van de wet van 13 december 2002 houdende verschillende wijzigingen van de kieswetgeving (bekendgemaakt in het Belgisch Staatsblad van 10 januari 2003), wegens schending van de artikelen 10 en 11 van de Grondwet.  

Die zaak is ingeschreven onder nummer 2621 van de rol van het Hof.  

De griffier,  
L. Potoms.  

COUR D’ARBITRAGE
[2003/200086]
Avis prescrit par l’article 74 de la loi spéciale du 6 janvier 1989 sur la Cour d’arbitrage

Par requête adressée à la Cour par lettre recommandée à la poste le 30 janvier 2003 et parvenue au greffe le 31 janvier 2003,  
J. Van den Driessche, demeurant à 1700 Dilbeek, Baron de Vironlaan 80, boîte 25, a introduit un recours en annulation et une demande de suspension de l’article 5 de la loi du 13 décembre 2002 modifiant le Code électoral ainsi que son annexe et de l’article 16 de la loi du 13 décembre 2002 portant diverses modifications en matière de législation électorale (publiées au Moniteur belge du 10 janvier 2003), pour cause de violation des articles 10 et 11 de la Constitution.  

Cette affaire est inscrite sous le numéro 2621 du rôle de la Cour.  

Le greffier,  
L. Potoms.  

SCHIEDSHOF
[2003/200086]
Bekanntmachung vorgeschrieben durch Artikel 74 des Sondergesetzes vom 6. Januar 1989 über den Schiedshof

Mit einer Klageschrift, die dem Hof mit am 30. Januar 2003 bei der Post aufgegebenem Einschreibebrief zugesandt wurde und am 31. Januar 2003 in der Kanzlei eingegangen ist, erhob J. Van den Driessche, wohnhaft in 1700 Dilbeek, Baron de Vironlaan 80 Bk. 25, Klage auf Nichtigerklärung und einstweilige Aufhebung von Artikel 5 des Gesetzes vom
13. Dezember 2002 zur Abänderung des Wahlgesetzbuches und seiner Anlage und von Artikel 16 des Gesetzes vom
13. Dezember 2002 zur Festlegung verschiedener Abänderungen der Wahlgesetzgebung (veröffentlicht im Belgischen Staatsblatt vom 10. Januar 2003), wegen Verstoßes gegen die Artikel 10 und 11 der Verfassung.  

Diese Rechtssache wurde unter der Nummer 2621 ins Geschäftsverzeichnis des Hofes eingetragen.  

Der Kanzler,  
L. Potoms.  

COUR D’ARBITRAGE
[2003/200081]
Avis prescrit par l’article 74 de la loi spéciale du 6 janvier 1989 sur la Cour d’arbitrage

Par arrêt du 3 décembre 2002 en cause du ministère public contre C. Guinchon et Y. Fourmeau, dont l’expédition est parvenue au greffe de la Cour d’arbitrage le 10 décembre 2002, la Cour d’appel de Mons a posé la question préjudicielle suivante:

« Les articles 10 et 11 de la Constitution, ainsi que l’article 6 de la Convention Européenne de Sauvegarde des Droits de l’Homme et des Libertés Fondamentales, sont-ils violés par les articles 67, §§ 1er et 2, du CWATUP, arrêté du 14 mai 1984, et 155, §§ 1er et 2, du CWATUP, décret du 27 novembre 1997, qui permettent au fonctionnaire délégué de l’administration de l’urbanisme et de l’aménagement du territoire de la Région wallonne d’intervenir au procès pénal pour y poursuivre, sans être titulaire de l’action publique et sans devoir se soumettre aux règles qui gouvernent la constitution de partie civile, une action qui ressortit à l’action publique et a pour objet une demande à caractère civil ? »
Cette affaire est inscrite sous le numéro 2582 du rôle de la Cour.  
Le greffier,  
P.-Y. Dutilleux.  

ARBITRAGEHOF
[2003/200081]
Bericht voorgeschreven bij artikel 74 van de bijzondere wet van 6 januari 1989 op het Arbitragehof

Bij arrest van 3 december 2002 in zake het openbaar ministerie tegen C. Guinchon en Y. Fourmeau, waarvan de expeditie ter griffie van het Arbitragehof is ingekomen op 10 december 2002, heeft het Hof van Beroep te Bergen de volgende prejudiciële vraag gesteld:

« Worden de artikelen 10 en 11 van de Grondwet, alsmede artikel 6 van het Europees Verdrag tot bescherming van de rechten van de mens en de fundamentele vrijheden geschonden door de artikelen 67, §§ 1 en 2 van het W.W.R.O.S.P., besluit van 14 mei 1984, en 155, §§ 1 en 2, van het W.W.R.O.S.P., decreet van 27 november 1997, die het een gemachtigde ambtenaar van de administratie stedenbouw en ruimtelijke ordening van het Waalse Gewest mogelijk maken tussen te komen in het strafproces om er, zonder houder te zijn van de strafvordering en zonder zich te moeten onderwerpen aan de regels betreffende de burgerlijke partijstelling, een zaak te vervolgen die onder de strafvordering valt en die een vordering van burgerlijke aard betreft ? »
Die zaak is ingeschreven onder nummer 2582 van de rol van het Hof.  
De griffier,  
P.-Y. Dutilleux.  

SCHIEDSHOF
[2003/200081]
Bekanntmachung vorgeschrieben durch Artikel 74 des Sondergesetzes vom 6. Januar 1989 über den Schiedshof

In seinem Urteil vom 3. Dezember 2002 in Sachen der Staatsanwaltschaft gegen C. Guinchon und Y. Fourmeau, dessen Ausfertigung am 10. Dezember 2002 in der Kanzlei des Schiedshofes eingegangen ist, hat der Appellationshof Mons folgende präjudizielle Frage gestellt:

«Wird gegen die Artikel 10 und 11 der Verfassung sowie gegen Artikel 6 der Europäischen Konvention zum Schutze der Menschenrechte und Grundfreiheiten verstoßen durch die Artikel 67 §§ 1 und 2 des Wallonischen Gesetzbuches über die Raumordnung, den Städtebau und das Erbe, Erlaß vom 14. Mai 1984, und 155 §§ 1 und 2 des Wallonischen Gesetzbuches über die Raumordnung, den Städtebau und das Erbe, Dekret vom 27. November 1997, die es einem beauftragten Beamten der Verwaltung für Raumordnung und Städtebau der Wallonischen Region ermöglichen, einem Strafprozeß beizutreten, um somit, ohne daß er die öffentliche Klage erhebt und ohne daß er den Regeln bezüglich der Klageerhebung als Zivilpartei unterliegen muß, ein Verfahren zu betreiben, das zum Bereich der öffentlichen Klage gehört und einen Anspruch zivilrechtlicher Art betrifft?»
Diese Rechtssache wurde unter der Nummer 2582 ins Geschäftsverzeichnis des Hofes eingetragen.  

Der Kanzler,  
P.-Y. Dutilleux.

By judgment of 3 December 2002 in the case of the public prosecutor against C. Guinchon and Y. Fourmeau, the copy of which was received at the registry of the Court of Arbitration on 10 December 2002, the Court of Appeal of Mons posed the following preliminary question:

"Are articles 10 and 11 of the Constitution, as well as article 6 of the European Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms, violated by articles 67, §§ 1 and 2, of the CWATUP, decree of 14 May 1984, and 155, §§ 1 and 2, of the CWATUP, decree of 27 November 1997, which allow the delegated official of the administration of urban planning and spatial planning of the Walloon Region to intervene in criminal proceedings to pursue there, without being the holder of the public action and without having to submit to the rules governing the constitution of civil party, an action which falls within the public action and has as its object a claim of a civil nature?"

On Thursday 30 January 2003, the Competition Council received notification of a concentration within the meaning of article 12, § 1, of the Act on the protection of economic competition, coordinated by Royal Decree of 1 July 1999 (Belgian Official Gazette of 1 September 1999) from which it appears that Deli Universal N.V. acquires exclusive control of Willemstein's Industriële Ondernemingen B.V., as well as its subsidiary JéWé Products N.V. and indirectly JéWé Trading N.V., through a share purchase and sale agreement concluded with WIO Holding B.V.

The Competition Council invites interested third parties to submit their possible observations on the concentration operation preferably before 18 February 2003.
These observations may be sent by fax or by post under the reference MEDE – C/C – 03/0005 to the following address: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Directorate of Commercial Policy, Corps of Rapporteurs, North Gate III, boulevard du Roi Albert II 16, B-1000 Brussels. Fax: 02-206 56 24.

D’une manie`re ge´ne´rale, les outils diamante´s sont utilise´s pour couper, forer ou traiter diffe´rents types de mate´riaux, parmi lesquels plusieurs sortes de be´ton, la brique, l’acier, le verre et l’asphalte. Dans leur notification, les parties ont cependant e´galement explique´ que, bien que pre´sentant des diffe´rences fonctionnelles, sous l’angle de l’offre, ces diffe´rents outils ont plusieurs caracte´ristiques communes. De ce fait, il existe un degre´ e´leve´ de substituabilite´ au niveau de l’offre en ce qui concerne la fabrication de ces outils dans le secteur de la construction. En ce qui concerne le segment de l’industrie de la pierre, les parties ont e´galement identifie´ quatre marche´s distincts:
—	les disques diamante´s; —	les caˆbles diamante´s; —	les plateaux de surfac¸age; —	et les lames d’armure. Ces lames sont spe´cifiquement destine´es aux scies a` lames multiples utilise´es pour la taille de la pierre et en particulier afin de trancher les blocs de pierre en dalles de dimension re´gulie`re. Les outils diamante´s utilise´s dans l’industrie de la pierre permettent de traiter la pierre naturelle depuis son extraction dans les carrie`res jusqu’a` son polissage final. Les parties estiment que ces quatre cate´gories d’outils constituent autant de marche´s distincts sous l’angle de la demande, meˆme si, comme c’est le cas pour le segment de la construction, on constate une re´elle substituabilite´ sous l’angle de l’offre. 3.2.3. Le secteur des diamants
Les diamants sont des pierres produites naturellement a` partir du carbone. Des de´couvertes scientifiques ont permis de produire des diamants artificiels. Ces diamants synthe´tiques sont fabrique´s par un proce´de´ industriel alliant haute tempe´rature et tre`s haute pression. Les multiples utilisations des diamants, tant synthe´tiques que naturels, sont regroupe´es dans deux cate´gories, a` savoir les diamants industriels et de joaillerie. 3.2.3.1. Les diamants industriels
Ces diamants (synthe´tiques ou naturels) sont utilise´s pour des applications industrielles (par exemple pour le forage pe´trolier ou minier) et sont vendus sous forme de me´langes ou blend. La plus grande partie des diamants industriels sont des diamants synthe´tiques. Dans de nombreuses applications industrielles, les diamants entrent en concurrence avec d’autres superabrasifs, tels que les nitrures de bore cubiques. Des parties a` la concentration, seule Diamant Boart via ses filiales Custodiam, est active sur ce marche´. Elle s’approvisionne aupre`s des principaux fabricants et les me´lange ensuite avec un savoir-faire particulier de´veloppe´ historiquement pour servir les besoins de sa maison me`re (a` raison de deux tiers). Le solde est vendu a` des tiers dont des socie´te´s qui faisaient anciennement partie du groupe Diamant Boart. Un me´lange diffe´rent permet une meilleure ade´quation a` l’application industrielle a` laquelle les diamants sont destine´s. Custodiam entre ainsi en concurrence avec ses fournisseurs qui de´veloppent e´galement des blends adapte´s aux besoin spe´cifiques de certaines applications industrielles. En Belgique, les ventes aux tiers se re´partissent en clients industriels et revendeurs qui livrent a` leur tour les utilisateurs c’est-a`-dire les fabricants d’outils abrasifs. Une grande proportion des diamants vendus a` ces interme´diaires est ensuite exporte´e a` des clients en dehors de la Belgique, selon Diamant Boart. 3.2.3.2. Les diamants de joaillerie

Un grand nombre de de´bouche´s dans le domaine de la joaillerie et des bijoux de fantaisie existe pour les diamants naturels et synthe´tiques. Eu e´gard a` l’absence de relations tant horizontales que verticales avec les autres marche´ en cause, ces activite´s ne sont pas plus amplement de´crites. La part de marche´ de Diamant Boart dans ce domaine, seule partie active, est extreˆmement faible. 3.3. Marche´ ge´ographique

Les marche´s en cause identifie´s ci-dessus ont une dimension europe´enne, voire plus e´tendue. En effet, comme le soulignent les Parties, les prix de ces produits comme la fac¸on dont ils sont vendus sont tre`s similaires a` travers toute l’Europe. En ce qui concerne tout particulie`rement le marche´ des diamants industriels, les parties ont insiste´ sur le fait que la fabrication de ces diamants se faisait en dehors de la zone europe´enne et qu’ils sont exporte´s dans de nombreuses re´gions du monde, graˆce en grande partie aux tre`s faible couˆ ts de transport (environ 2 % du prix) et aux droits douaniers tre`s limite´s. La taille mondiale de ce marche´ a par ailleurs e´te´ reconnue par le Conseil de la concurrence dans plusieurs affaires re´centes. 4. Analyse concurrentielle

Les parties ont fourni dans leur notification plusieurs tableaux. Ceux-ci reprennent les valeurs de chaque marche´ de produits en cause impliquant au moins une des parties en cause ainsi que les ventes et parts de marche´ respectives re´alise´es dans ces marche´s par les parties et leurs concurrents. 4.1.1. Competition Council. — Decision No. 2002-C/C-32 of 18 April 2002
Case CONC-C/C-02/0015 - Autoliv Inc. - Visteon Corporation
Having regard to the notification of the concentration operation filed with the secretariat of the Competition Council on 4 March 2002. Having regard to the Report of the Corps of Reporters of 27 March 2002. Having heard at the hearing of 18 April 2002 the Reporter in his report. Although duly summoned, the parties did not consider it necessary to be heard by the Competition Council and, by letter of 12 April 2002, acquiesced to the conclusions of the report. A. The parties concerned The acquirer
Autoliv Inc. is a company incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware, United States, and whose executive headquarters is located in Stockholm, Sweden. It develops, manufactures and markets automotive restraint systems. It owns a production unit in Belgium, Autoliv Belgium N.V., whose registered office is located at Mai Zetterlingstraat 70, 9042 Gent [business secret]. Autoliv acquired the automotive safety unit of Morton International in 1997. The seller
Visteon Corporation is a company incorporated under the laws of the State of Delaware, United States and established in Dearborn, in the State of Michigan, United States of America. It also manufactures and markets automotive restraint systems. The target company
The operations acquired are the North American and European activities of restraint electronic components of Visteon Corporation (United States, Canada and Portugal). B. The notified operation
Autoliv proposes to acquire part of the restraint electronic components assets of Visteon in North America and Europe. This unit produces and sells airbag control electronic components. Both parties produce and sell these products, but Autoliv is not active in this market in Belgium. This transaction will enable Autoliv to establish itself in the United States where it is not yet active, unlike Visteon. The aforementioned companies are undertakings within the meaning of Article 1 of the Act and the notified operation is a concentration operation within the meaning of Article 9 of the Act. On the basis of the information provided by the parties, the turnover thresholds referred to in Article 11 of the Act are met. C. The markets concerned
The economic sector concerned by the concentration is that of the manufacture of parts and accessories for motor vehicles (NACE code 34.3), but also that of the trade in automotive equipment (NACE code: 50.3). 1. Product markets concerned
On a global level, both parties develop, manufacture and market airbag control electronic components. These consist of an electronic control unit comprising a detector. They are integrated into vehicles where they are connected, via a cable, to the airbag module which they trigger in the event of an impact such as an accident. Airbag modules consist of a gas generator and a bag in a plastic cover integrated into the steering wheel or dashboard. Airbag modules and airbag control electronic components are sophisticated products individually adapted to each vehicle model. For safety and quality reasons, no replacement market for airbag control electronic components exists and all spare parts are supplied by the original automobile manufacturer who, in turn, obtains them directly from the airbag system supplier. Automobile manufacturers, as a general rule, purchase airbag control electronic components separately from airbag modules. They prefer to perform the integration of the products themselves, insofar as this allows them to increase their flexibility in terms of technology and price. In accordance with the approach adopted by the European Commission in application of the Merger Regulation, the parties consider the manufacture and marketing of airbag control electronic components as a distinct market (cf. decisions No. IV/M.686, Nokia/Autoliv of 05/02/1996 and No. IV/M.872, TRW/Magna of 01/01/1997). Consequently, the product market in question that may be retained is that of the manufacture and marketing of airbag control electronic components. 2. Geographic market concerned
The geographic market consists of the entire Belgian territory. The parties note, however, that the geographic market is in reality at least the European Economic Area. D. Competitive analysis
1. Structure of supply and demand
The value of the market for the manufacture and marketing of airbag control electronic components in Belgium is [business secret] Mio $ according to Siemens [business secret]. Autoliv does not sell airbag control electronic components in Belgium. There is therefore no market affected by the operation in this case. Besides Visteon, two other companies are present in the market in question in Belgium, namely Bosch and Siemens. The parties estimate their market shares as follows:
VISTEON: [business secret] % SIEMENS: [business secret] % BOSCH: [business secret] %
Siemens attributes to Visteon a market share of the order of [business secret] % in Belgium and evaluates its market share at [business secret] % based on the figures mentioned in doc. 4 ([business secret]). [business secret]
According to the parties, Autoliv has a market share of [business secret] % at European level, while the Acquired Operations represent approximately [business secret] %. 2. Assessment
Since Autoliv is not present in the market in question, the parties' market shares will remain unchanged after the operation. Moreover, no party questioned by the Competition Service makes any comments regarding this concentration. The Council therefore considers that the notified concentration will not have the effect of creating or strengthening a dominant position which significantly impedes effective competition in the Belgian market in question or in a substantial part thereof. FOR THESE REASONS
The Competition Council
Finds that the concentration falls within the scope of the Act of 5 August 1991 on the protection of economic competition and is admissible pursuant to Articles 33 § 1 and 33, § 2, 1.a, of that Act. Thus decided on 18 April 2002 by the chamber of the Competition Council composed of Mrs Marie-Claude Grégoire, Chamber President, Mr Patrick De Wolf,  
Mr Pierre Battard and Mr Roger Ramaekers, Members. *

Competition Council. — Decision No. 2002-C/C-44 of 13 June 2002
Case CONC-C/C-02/0026: VMS-Keytrade.Com S.A. – RealBank S.A. Having regard to the concentration notification filed on 29 April 2002; Having regard to the reporter's report of 24 May 2002; Having heard at the hearing of 13 June 2002:
—	Mr Patrick Marchand, reporter; —	Mr Henri Delwaide, lawyer registered with the French-speaking and German-speaking bar of Brussels, common representative of the notifying parties. 1. The notifying parties
1.1. Absorbing undertaking:
VMS-Keytrade.Com S.A. (hereinafter VMS) is a public limited company under Belgian law with its registered office at boulevard du Souverain 100, 1170 Brussels, and registered in the Brussels trade register under number 627.795. Its purpose is to make available to its clients, natural or legal persons, private or institutional, stockbroking companies or banks, both in Belgium and abroad, tools enabling them to manage their own portfolio, in real time or deferred, by electronic means in general and via the Internet network in particular. The company VMS, in practice, concentrates its activities on offering an intermediation (brokerage) service relating to the execution of stock exchange orders. Orders may be transmitted to the company by telephone, fax, mail or directly online via the Internet. In the market for stock transaction execution services (on Euronext Brussels), its market share is less than [business secret] %. However, its status as a stockbroking company did not allow it to be a full-fledged bank. 1.2. Absorbed undertaking:
RealBank S.A. (hereinafter RealBank) is a public limited company under Belgian law with its registered office at rue des Colonies 1, 1000 Brussels, and registered in the Brussels trade register under number 81.690. Its purpose is banking operations, financial operations, brokerage and commission. It may carry out all undertakings and operations relating directly or indirectly to its purpose or likely to promote its achievement. The company may hold partnership shares and participations within the limits provided by the legal status of banks. Specifically, this company offers a complete range of banking services, with the exception of credit which remains a marginal activity [business secret]. In the ranking of all Belgian banks established according to the total amount of "customer deposits", Realbank occupied, in 2000, ["between 50th and 100th position" - business secret]. In the market for stock transaction execution services (on Euronext Brussels), its market share is less than 2%. 2. Description of the operation
The notification concerns a concentration operation by which VMS wishes to absorb RealBank and its subsidiaries by means of a merger by absorption. According to the notifying parties, the purpose of this concentration is to create a new banking group targeting the "retail" sector in Belgium and progressively offering a complete range of banking products. However, even after the merger, the new company will not have the necessary means to compete with the large network banks with "retail" customers. Consequently, its strategy will consist mainly of approaching the customer directly, by all distance marketing techniques (Internet, mailing, affinity groups, etc.). The objective is therefore to create a "direct" bank, similar to what certain well-established competitors have achieved (DHB Bank, Dexia-Cortal, Deutsche Bank-Bank24, Citibank, Banque Delen, Robeco Bank Belgium, etc.). This merger is subject to the prior approval of the Banking and Finance Commission. 3. Scope of application
The aforementioned companies are undertakings within the meaning of Article 1 of the Act and the notified operation is a concentration operation within the meaning of Article 9 of the Act. As provided in Article 46, § 3, a), of the Act, for banks, credit institutions and other financial institutions, turnover is replaced by one-tenth of total balance sheets, which corresponds respectively for the VMS and RealBank groups to € 9.2 million and € 23.9 million. Article 11 of the Act provides that the concentration falls within the scope of the Act where the undertakings concerned together achieve in Belgium a turnover of more than 40 million euros and at least two of the undertakings concerned each achieve in Belgium a turnover of at least 15 million euros. In the present case, the companies VMS and Realbank do not together reach in Belgium the threshold of 40 million euros required by Article 11 of the Act. Moreover, VMS does not reach the threshold of 15 million euros required in Belgium. The thresholds referred to in Article 11 of the Act are therefore not met. FOR THESE REASONS
The Competition Council
— Finds that the concentration does not fall within the scope of the Act of 5 August 1991 on the protection of economic competition and therefore did not need to be notified. Thus decided on 13 June 2002 by the chamber of the Competition Council composed of
Mrs Marie-Claude Grégoire (chamber president),  
Mr Patrick De Wolf, Mrs Dominique Smeets and Mr Roger Ramaekers, Members. *

Competition Council. — Decision No. 2002-C/C-46 of 26 June 2002
Case No. CONC-C/C-02/0027. - AB Electrolux/Diamant Boart International s.a. Having regard to the concentration notification filed by the notifying parties with the secretariat of the Competition Council on 8 May 2002. Having regard to the report filed by Patrick Marchand on behalf of the corps of reporters dated 7 June 2002. Having heard at the hearing of 26 June 2002:
—	Mr Patrick Marchand, reporter. —	Messrs Dirk Vandermeersch and Marc Waha, common representatives of the notifying parties
1. The notifying parties
1.1. The acquirer
AB Electrolux (publ) is a company under Swedish law established at 143 S:t. Göransgatan SE-105 45 in Stockholm, Sweden, whose shares are listed on several stock exchanges, including Stockholm and London. It is active on a global scale in several sectors: kitchen and catering appliances (cooking systems, dishwashers, refrigerators, etc.), cleaning appliances (vacuum cleaners, industrial washing machines, etc.) and outdoor work for private and professional use (hedge trimmers, chainsaws, garden tractors, lawnmowers, etc.). Electrolux is also active through its subsidiary Dimas AB in the manufacture of diamond cutting machines intended for the construction industry. Dimas AB also manufactures diamond abrasive tools (diamond tools) that can equip the machines it produces but also those produced by other manufacturers. In Belgium, Electrolux's activity in the diamond cutting sector is limited to wall saws and diamond tools (diamond discs) intended for certain types of saws, and only for use in the construction sector. 1.2. The sellers
The sellers concerned in the present operation number 22. They are the shareholders of Diamant Boart International composed of natural persons and legal persons including a company listed on the London stock exchange (Candover Investments plc). 1.3. The target undertaking
Diamant Boart International is a public limited company under Belgian law. It is established at avenue du Pont de Luttre 74, 1190 Brussels, and is registered in the Brussels trade register under No. 638.636. The activity of this undertaking is divided into three main areas:
—	the manufacture and sale of diamond cutting machines intended for the construction industry
—	the manufacture and sale of diamond tools, intended mainly for cutting machines in the construction industry, in the stone industry and in the ceramics industry; and
—	the sale of industrial diamonds and jewellery diamonds. This activity is carried out by two subsidiaries, Custodiam sa (Belgian undertaking) and Custodiam (Xiamen) co., Ltd. which is a Chinese undertaking (hereinafter, for these two subsidiaries, Custodiam). 2. The notified operation
The notification concerns a concentration operation by which AB Electrolux (hereinafter Electrolux) wishes to acquire exclusive control of Diamant Boart International s.a. (hereinafter Diamant Boart). This notification follows a share transfer agreement signed on 2 May 2002 under which the Sellers transfer to Electrolux all the shares they hold in Diamant Boart. The envisaged operation aims to enable Electrolux to enter new segments of the diamond cutting industry and thus to compete with the main producers active in this market. Moreover, the operation will enable Electrolux to acquire a certain presence in certain regions of the world where it is not yet active in this field. The operation has also been notified in Austria, Germany, Ireland, Italy, Finland, Czech Republic, Brazil and the United States. The aforementioned companies are undertakings within the meaning of Article 1 of the Act and the notified operation is a concentration operation within the meaning of Article 9 of the Act. With regard to the concentration operation as notified, it appears that Electrolux achieved in Belgium a consolidated turnover of approximately [confidential] million euros (of which less than 0.1% in the sector concerned by the operation) and that the target undertaking, Diamant Boart, achieved in Belgium a consolidated turnover of approximately [confidential] million euros. On the basis of the information provided by the parties, the turnover thresholds referred to in Article 11 are therefore met. 3. Market in question
3.1. Economic sector concerned
The economic sectors concerned by the concentration are:
—	the sector of diamond cutting machines and corresponding diamond tools (nace code 29 405); —	the diamond sector (nace code 36.221 and 51.561). 3.2. Product market in question
The parties initially identify three relevant sectors of activity:
—	the diamond cutting machines sector; —	the diamond tools sector; —	the diamond sector. 3.2.1. The diamond cutting machines sector
These machines are devices used to cut, sharpen, drill or polish hard materials. They are composed of an independent abrasive mechanism (called cutting tools) in order to be easily replaced when necessary. Cutting machines can be divided into three segments according to the sector of activity in which these machines are used:
—	construction; —	the stone industry; —	ceramics cutting. The parties consider that this distinction is necessary both from the demand side and from the supply side (the technical characteristics of the machines, their operation, the customers,...). 3.2.1.1. The stone and ceramics industry
Since the parties do not manufacture cutting machines in these sectors, there is no need to further examine these segments. 3.2.1.2. The construction industry
The parties consider that this sector is composed of seven distinct markets, seven categories of cutting machines that can be equipped with abrasive tools:
—	floor saws; —	wall saws; —	table saws; —	portable saws; —	wire cutting machines; —	drills; —	and surfacing devices. This distinction is necessary, according to the parties, because these machines are designed for a particular use, the final consumer generally does not use a machine designed for a certain type of work in the context of an application normally requiring another type of machine. These devices are moreover manufactured by different production lines that use equipment specific to them, having regard to their shape, size and engine power. 3.2.2. The diamond tools sector
The parties consider that these tools, intended to be used with appropriate cutting machines, may compete with conventional abrasive tools. However, given the envisaged operation, the parties did not consider it necessary to examine in more detail the degree of substitution between diamond tools and conventional tools since by adopting a narrow market definition limited to diamond tools, the envisaged operation does not generate the creation or strengthening of a dominant position. The following description therefore concerns only diamond tools. This sector, like that of cutting machines, can be divided into three segments according to the sector of activity in which these tools are used:
—	construction; —	the stone industry; —	ceramics cutting. In this sector, the parties are active in the construction segment as well as in the stone industry segment. Since Electrolux and Diamant Boart are not present in the ceramics cutting segment, the latter will not be addressed. With regard to the construction segment, the parties have identified four distinct markets:
—	diamond discs. These discs for circular saws can be used and adapted to floor saws, wall saws, table saws and portable saws. These discs are interchangeable to a large extent; —	diamond wires. Diamond wires are mainly used in the construction sector to cut various types of concrete. The use of this type of wire constitutes a different cutting technique; —	drill bits. The use of bits is only intended for drilling operations. They are therefore not substitutable for other forms of diamond tools; —	surfacing plates. These tools are exclusively used to polish, clean, or level dirty or rough surfaces, or to remove surface layers (for example mastic, resin,...). Generally speaking, diamond tools are used to cut, drill or treat different types of materials, including several types of concrete, brick, steel, glass and asphalt. In their notification, however, the parties also explained that, although presenting functional differences, from the supply side, these different tools have several common characteristics. As a result, there is a high degree of substitutability at the supply level with regard to the manufacture of these tools in the construction sector. With regard to the stone industry segment, the parties have also identified four distinct markets:
—	diamond discs; —	diamond wires; —	surfacing plates; —	and gang saw blades. These blades are specifically intended for multi-blade saws used for stone cutting and in particular to slice stone blocks into slabs of regular dimension. Diamond tools used in the stone industry make it possible to process natural stone from its extraction in quarries to its final polishing. The parties consider that these four categories of tools constitute as many distinct markets from the demand side, even if, as is the case for the construction segment, there is real substitutability from the supply side. 3.2.3. The diamond sector
Diamonds are stones produced naturally from carbon. Scientific discoveries have made it possible to produce artificial diamonds. These synthetic diamonds are manufactured by an industrial process combining high temperature and very high pressure. The multiple uses of diamonds, both synthetic and natural, are grouped into two categories, namely industrial and jewellery diamonds. 3.2.3.1. Industrial diamonds
These diamonds (synthetic or natural) are used for industrial applications (for example for oil or mining drilling) and are sold in the form of mixtures or blends. The vast majority of industrial diamonds are synthetic diamonds. In many industrial applications, diamonds compete with other superabrasives, such as cubic boron nitrides. Of the parties to the concentration, only Diamant Boart through its subsidiaries Custodiam is active in this market. It sources from the main manufacturers and then mixes them with particular know-how developed historically to serve the needs of its parent company (at a rate of two-thirds). The balance is sold to third parties including companies that were formerly part of the Diamant Boart group. A different mixture allows better adaptation to the industrial application for which the diamonds are intended. Custodiam thus competes with its suppliers who also develop blends adapted to the specific needs of certain industrial applications. In Belgium, sales to third parties are divided into industrial customers and resellers who in turn supply users, i.e. manufacturers of abrasive tools. A large proportion of the diamonds sold to these intermediaries is then exported to customers outside Belgium, according to Diamant Boart. 3.2.3.2. Jewellery diamonds

A large number of outlets in the field of jewellery and costume jewellery exist for natural and synthetic diamonds. Given the absence of both horizontal and vertical relationships with the other markets in question, these activities are not further described. Diamant Boart's market share in this field, the only active party, is extremely low. 3.3. Geographic market

The markets in question identified above have a European dimension, or even wider. Indeed, as the Parties point out, the prices of these products and the way they are sold are very similar throughout Europe. With regard particularly to the market for industrial diamonds, the parties emphasized that the manufacture of these diamonds takes place outside the European zone and that they are exported to many regions of the world, thanks largely to very low transport costs (approximately 2% of the price) and very limited customs duties. The global size of this market has moreover been recognized by the Competition Council in several recent cases. 4. Competitive analysis

L’ope´ration qui fait l’objet de la pre´sente notification consiste en la reprise par ECS (constitue´e le 12 décembre 2001 et filiale a` 100 % d’Electrabel), de la cliente`le d’Ideg portant sur la fourniture d’e´lectricite´ aux clients de celle-ci au fur et a` mesure qu’ils deviennent e´ligibles et dans la mesure ou` ils ne de´cident pas de conclure un contrat avec un autre fournisseur. On entend par client e´ligible le client qui a le droit de conclure un contrat de fourniture avec l’entreprise de son choix et pour ce faire a un droit d’acce`s au re´seau. La reprise par ECS de cette cliente`le e´ligible d’Ideg vise´e par cette notification n’a pas fait l’objet d’un document spe´cifique mais doit se de´duire d’un ensemble de documents parmi lesquels le document intitule´ « Me´morandum of Understanding entre Intermix – Electrabel signe´ le 30 mars 2001 » et les modifications apporte´es aux statuts d’Ideg adopte´es le 19 avril 2002. Le conseil d’administration d’Ideg a, le 6 juin 2001, de´cide´ a` l’unanimite´ de faire adhe´rer leur intercommunale au Me´morandum of Understanding. En contrepartie de cette cession de cliente`le par Ideg, les communes se voient offrir la possibilite´ d’augmenter leur actionnariat dans l’intercommunale a` des conditions avantageuses ainsi que de participer aux be´ne´fices de ECS dans une mesure plus grande que le montant d’actions de´tenues dans celle-ci. La participation des communes dans la socie´te´ ECS sera en effet limite´e a` 5 % de son capital, mais donnera droit a` une participation aux be´ne´fices a` concurrence de 40 % du re´sultat. 3. De´lais
La notification a e´te´ effectue´e le 22 mai 2002. Le de´lai vise´ a` l’article 33 de la loi expire en application de l’article 33,

Competition Council. — Decision no. 2002-C/C-49 of 28 June 2002
Case CONC-C/C-02/29: ELECTRABEL CUSTOMER SOLUTIONS S.A./IDEG S.C.R.L. In the matter of:
Electrabel Customer Solutions S.A. (hereinafter ECS), having its registered office at boulevard du Régent 8, 1000 Brussels, and
Intercommunale de Distribution d'Electricité et de Gaz having taken the form of an S.C.R.L. (hereinafter Ideg), having its registered office at 5000 Namur, avenue Albert Ier 19; Having regard to the law of 5 August 1991 on the protection of economic competition coordinated on 1 July 1999 (hereinafter LPCE); Having regard to the notification dated 21 May 2002 of a concentration which consists of the takeover by ECS, a subsidiary of Electrabel, of the clientele of the intercommunale Ideg as and when it becomes eligible; Having regard to the documents in the file of the Competition Service; Having regard to the reasoned report of the Corps of Rapporteurs dated 12 June 2002; Having regard to the decision on the confidentiality of the documents in the file of 17 June 2002; Having regard to the request submitted on the basis of article 32quater, § 2 LPCE, on 13 June 2002 by S.A. Luminus to be heard in this procedure; Having regard to the decision of 18 June 2002 granting this request; Having regard to the request submitted on the basis of article 32quater, § 2 LPCE, on 17 June 2002 by N.V. Nuon Energy Trade & Wholesale to be heard in this procedure; Having regard to the decision of 19 June 2002 granting this request; Having regard to the request dated 20 June 2002 and transmitted to the Competition Council on 21 June 2002 by which the Commission for Electricity and Gas Regulation (abbreviated CREG) requests on the basis of article 32quater, § 2 LPCE and article 23 of the law of 29 April 1999 on the organisation of the electricity market, to be heard in this procedure; Having regard to the decision of 24 June 2002 granting this request; Having heard at the hearing of 26 June 2002, S.A. Luminus and Nuon Energy Trade & Wholesale and the Commission for Electricity and Gas Regulation; Having heard at the hearing of 27 June 2002 Mr rapporteur P. Marchand and the notifying parties represented by
Mr de Garcia and Mr Baeten and assisted by Mr Vandencasteele, Mr Brinckman and Mr Vronincks, lawyers in Brussels; 1. the notifying parties
1.1. Acquirer
The company Electrabel Customer Solutions (hereinafter ECS) is a public limited company under Belgian law incorporated by deed of 12 December 2001 published in the annexes to the Moniteur belge of 28 December 2001, having its registered office at 1000 Brussels, boulevard du Régent 8, and having as its object the supply of electricity and gas as well as the supply of related products and services. This company is in fact a 100% subsidiary of Electrabel S.A. The public limited company under Belgian law Electrabel having its registered office at 1000 Brussels, boulevard du Régent 8, is a company active at all stages in the electricity sector, from production to supply to the final customer. 1.2. Seller
The Intercommunale de Distribution d'Energie et de Gaz (hereinafter Ideg) is an intercommunal association having taken the form of a cooperative company with limited liability, established to ensure the distribution of electricity and gas to customers located in the territory of the affiliated municipalities of the province of Namur and two municipalities in Hainaut. Its registered office is established in Namur, avenue Albert Ier 19. Ideg is a mixed intercommunale. It is established on the basis of a partnership with a private company, namely Electrabel, currently the majority shareholder (to the extent of 62.25%). The municipalities associated with it hold 37.75% of its capital. Regulatory provisions and in particular the provisions of the decree of 5 December 1996 on Walloon intercommunales, however provide that the municipalities always have the majority of votes as well as the presidency in the management and control bodies, regardless of the proportion of the contributions of the various parties to the constitution of the capital. 1.3. Target undertaking or part of undertaking
The operation targets Ideg's clientele becoming eligible in the electricity supply market. 2. Description of the operation
2.1. Preamble
The notified concentration concerns the electricity market which is currently in full liberalisation phase. This liberalisation of the electricity market was decided at European level by directive 96/92 of 19 December 1996 which imposes a limited and progressive opening of the electricity market. This liberalisation is accompanied by regulation which pays particular attention to network access. Energy in Belgium is a matter whose powers are divided between the federal authority and the Regions. Very schematically, this distribution of powers is established as follows:
—	the federal State is competent with regard to production, transmission and tariffs; —	distribution and supply are regional matters. The normative framework in this matter comprises:
—	the law of 29 April 1999 on the organisation of the electricity market (hereinafter electricity law) published in the Moniteur belge of 11 May 1999; —	the decree of the Flemish Region of 17 July 2000 on the organisation of the electricity market (hereinafter
Flemish decree); —	the decree of the Walloon Region of 12 April 2001 on the organisation of the regional electricity market (hereinafter Walloon decree) and the order of the Walloon Government of 21 March 2002 on customers who have become eligible and the control of their eligibility; —	the ordinance of 19 July 2001 on the organisation of the electricity market in the Brussels-Capital Region (hereinafter the Ordinance). The different levels of competence have adopted their own market opening schedules. These differ both in terms of eligibility thresholds and dates. At the end of this liberalisation of the electricity market in Belgium, electricity distribution should be split into two activities to be entrusted to separate companies:
—	network management, which concerns the operation, maintenance and development of the distribution network. The network manager must concentrate on its core activity. It may not carry out production activities - other than green electricity - nor sales activities - other than sales to captive clientele and sales to so-called protected clientele; —	the sale of electricity which concerns the supply of energy to eligible customers. However, as early as 1996, municipalities in partnership with Electrabel had decided to continue, within mixed intercommunales, network management and sales activities to clientele under municipal monopoly. Mixed intercommunales thus currently ensure the management of the distribution network as well as the supply of electricity. However, article 8, § 1 of the Walloon decree on the organisation of the regional electricity market applicable to Ideg expressly provides that the distribution network manager may not carry out production activities other than green electricity or electricity sales other than sales necessitated by its activity as network manager. The distribution network manager may not engage in supply activities to eligible customers nor in the supply of other services on the electricity market which are not directly linked to the performance of the tasks referred to in article 11 (that is to say network management). However, at the request of the municipalities, the distribution network manager may supply electricity to captive customers…. It follows that Walloon mixed intercommunales, such as Ideg, which wish to be designated as network manager, will no longer be able to simultaneously supply electricity to (become) eligible customers. Given the implications of the ongoing liberalisation process, Electrabel and Intermixt Wallonie (public utility establishment grouping all public representatives of mixed intercommunales) have thus negotiated the terms of a new agreement capable of maintaining their partnership in a balanced framework. The principle adopted is that the municipalities and the intercommunales will become more involved in network management, monopolistic and regulated type activities, while Electrabel will concentrate primarily on the activity of supplying customers. This specialisation of each is not exclusive: the municipalities via the intercommunales will continue to have an interest in the result of the electricity marketing company and Electrabel will retain a participation - minority but significant - in the capital of the distribution network managers whose operation it will continue to ensure. In order to valorise the clientele that these intercommunales currently supply with electricity and which they will no longer be able to supply upon their eligibility, the municipalities have agreed with their partner within the mixed intercommunales, Electrabel, that a company ECS, established in December 2001 and whose shares are entirely held by Electrabel, will take over this clientele. In consideration for this takeover of control by ECS and this transfer of clientele by Ideg, the municipalities are offered the possibility of increasing their shareholding in the intercommunale. These municipalities will also become minority shareholders (maximum 5% of capital) in this company ECS and will participate in the profits to the extent of 40% of the result achieved. These negotiations resulted in the development of various agreements and a Memorandum of Understanding signed on 30 March 2001. 2.2. Operation covered by the notification
The operation which is the subject of this notification consists of the takeover by ECS (established on 12 December 2001 and a 100% subsidiary of Electrabel), of Ideg's clientele concerning the supply of electricity to its customers as and when they become eligible and insofar as they do not decide to conclude a contract with another supplier. An eligible customer means the customer who has the right to conclude a supply contract with the company of his choice and for this purpose has a right of access to the network. The takeover by ECS of this eligible clientele of Ideg covered by this notification was not the subject of a specific document but must be deduced from a set of documents including the document entitled "Memorandum of Understanding between Intermix – Electrabel signed on 30 March 2001" and the amendments made to Ideg's articles of association adopted on 19 April 2002. The board of directors of Ideg decided unanimously on 6 June 2001 to have their intercommunale adhere to the Memorandum of Understanding. In consideration for this transfer of clientele by Ideg, the municipalities are offered the possibility of increasing their shareholding in the intercommunale on advantageous terms as well as participating in the profits of ECS to a greater extent than the amount of shares held in it. The municipalities' participation in the company ECS will in fact be limited to 5% of its capital, but will give entitlement to a participation in profits to the extent of 40% of the result. 3. Time limits
The notification was made on 22 May 2002. The time limit referred to in article 33 of the law expires in application of article 33,

### §§ 1er et 2 de la LPCE, le 5 juillet 2002

4. Champ d’application
Les socie´te´s ECS et Ideg sont des entreprises au sens de l’article 1er de la LPCE. Apre`s la concentration, ECS de´tiendra le controˆle exclusif de l’activite´ d’Ideg de fourniture d’e´lectricite´ aux clients e´ligibles (ou qui le deviendront). L’ope´ration consiste donc a` une concentration au sens de l’article 9, § 1er, de la loi. Sur la base des chiffres fournis par les parties dans la notification, les seuils des chiffres d’affaires vise´s a` l’article 11 de la loi sont atteints. 5. Marche´ concerne´
5.1. Secteur e´conomique concerne´
Le secteur e´conomique concerne´ par la concentration est celui de la production et de la distribution d’e´lectricite´ (code NACE: 40.1). 5.2. Marche´ de produits concerne´
Dans le secteur de l’e´lectricite´, cinq types d’activite´s diffe´rentes peuvent eˆtre distingue´s, soit la ge´ne´ration, le transport, la distribution, la fourniture et le ne´goce. —	La ge´ne´ration consiste en la production d’e´lectricite´. —	Le transport est l’acheminement de l’e´lectricite´ sur des caˆbles de haute tension. —	La distribution est l’acheminement de l’e´lectricite´ sur des caˆbles de moyenne et basse tension. —	La fourniture consiste en la livraison au consommateur final. —	Le ne´goce est l’achat et la revente d’e´lectricite´. Les quatre premie`res activite´s peuvent eˆtre conside´re´es comme relevant de marche´s de produits distincts, puisque celles-ci ne´cessitent des actifs et des ressources diffe´rents et parce que les conditions de marche´ et de concurrence sont diffe´rentes pour chacune d’entre elles. Quant au ne´goce d’e´lectricite´, la question de savoir s’il constitue un marche´ distinct du ne´goce ge´ne´ral des produits d’e´nergie a e´te´ laisse´e ouverte par la Commission europe´enne. Ce marche´ ne constituant pas un marche´ concerne´ pour la pre´sente, il n’y a pas lieu de se prononcer sur cette question. Fourniture d’e´lectricite´
Suite a` la libe´ralisation d’une partie du marche´ de l’e´lectricite´ initie´e par la directive CE 96/92, une distinction supple´mentaire doit eˆtre faite entre la fourniture d’e´lectricite´ aux clients e´ligibles et non e´ligibles (ou captifs,  
c.a`.d. qui ne peuvent pas choisir leur fournisseur). Ceux-ci rele`vent de deux marche´s de produits distincts, dans la mesure ou` les conditions de concurrence sont diffe´rentes, et ou` , le plus souvent, ils sont soumis a` des re´glementations spe´cifiques. C’est dans ce contexte que s’inscrit la pre´sente ope´ration puisque, en vertu de l’article 8, § 1er, du de´cret wallon, le gestionnaire du re´seau de distribution se voit interdire toute activite´ de fourniture aux clients e´ligibles. Ce gestionnaire du re´seau sera probablement l’intercommunale ou une nouvelle filiale de celle-ci cre´e´e a` cet effet. Electrabel est active directement ou indirectement sur les marche´s de production, de transport, de distribution, de fourniture d’e´lectricite´ et de ne´goce de produits lie´s a` l’e´lectricite´. Ideg est active sur les marche´s de la distribution et de la fourniture d’e´lectricite´. Cette dernie`re activite´, pour autant qu’elle concerne les clients devenant e´ligibles n’ayant pas choisi de fournisseur, sera exerce´e par ECS, filiale a` 100 % d’ Electrabel. Par conse´quent, le marche´ de produits concerne´ est celui de la fourniture d’e´lectricite´ aux clients e´ligibles. 5.3. Marche´ ge´ographique concerne´
Le marche´ ge´ographique est au maximum national. En effet, compte tenu des proble`mes lie´s aux capacite´s limite´es des interconnexions, les importations sont restreintes dans une mesure assez significative. 6. Analyse concurrentielle
6.1. Structure de l’offre: Position dominante d’Electrabel
Electrabel occupe une position privile´gie´e sur le marche´ belge puisqu’il de´tient des parts de marche´ extreˆmement e´leve´es quel que soit le marche´ envisage´. 6.1.1. Fourniture
Le marche´ de la fourniture d’e´lectricite´ aux clients e´ligibles en Belgique est estime´ par les parties en volume (GWh) a` 30.962,4 pour l’anne´e 2001. La part de marche´ d’Electrabel s’e´le`ve a` plus de 90 %. Aucun autre concurrent, quelle que soit sa puissance e´conomique et financie`re (EDF, RWE,  
E.ON), ne posse`de individuellement une part de marche´ supe´rieure ou e´gale a` 5 %. 6.1.2. Production
La position dominante d’Electrabel sur le marche´ de la fourniture aux clients e´ligibles doit e´galement eˆtre examine´e en tenant compte de la situation quasi monopolistique d’Electrabel sur le marche´ de la production en Belgique. Depuis 1995, la S.A. Electrabel et la S.A. SPE sont regroupe´es au sein d’une socie´te´ coope´rative (CPTE) dont le but est d’assurer la coordination de la production et du transport de l’e´nergie e´lectrique des deux entreprises. Electrabel y est actionnaire a` concurrence de 91,5 %. Sur une production totale en 2001 estime´e a` 75.953 GWh par la CREG et a` [secrets d’affaires] GWh par les parties notifiantes, [secrets d’affaires] GWh ont e´te´ produits par Electrabel, soit une part de marche´ de [plus de 90 % - le pourcentage exact rele`ve du secret des affaires]. Aucune e´volution significative n’est a` pre´voir, ni a` court et ni a` moyen terme sur ce marche´. Elle tendrait meˆme a` conforter la position d’Electrabel. Cette situation pose d’autant plus de proble`mes que les importations d’e´lectricite´ sont d’un niveau assez faible. 6.2. Transport
L’activite´ de transport concerne l’acheminement de l’e´lectricite´ sur le re´seau haute tension. La socie´te´ coope´rative CPTE, filiale d’Electrabel et de la SPE, e´tait proprie´taire de la majeure partie du re´seau de haute tension en Belgique et en assurait la gestion. Le 28 juin 2001, le re´seau haute tension a e´te´ apporte´ a` une socie´te´ filiale de CPTE, la socie´te´ ELIA. Cette dernie`re sera le gestionnaire du re´seau de transport dont la de´signation, les missions et le controˆle sont re´gle´s par la loi e´lectricite´ et les arreˆte´s d’exe´cution. 6.3. Distribution
Electrabel dispose e´galement d’une position privile´gie´e au niveau de la distribution (acheminement de l’e´lectricite´ depuis le re´seau de transport jusqu’au consommateur sur un re´seau a` moyenne et basse tension). En effet, les activite´s de distribution rele`vent du monopole des communes qui pour la plupart se sont rassemble´es au sein d’intercommu-nales. Ces intercommunales sont pour la majorite´ d’entre elles qualifie´es de mixtes car elles comptent un associe´ prive´, en l’espe`ce dans tous les cas Electrabel qui est actionnaire ge´ne´ralement majoritaire. Ainsi, les 16 intercommunales mixtes dans lesquelles Electrabel est actionnaire regroupent plus de 500 communes et desservent quotidiennement plus de 8 millions d’habitants en Belgique, soit plus de 82 % de l’e´lectricite´ distribue´e. 6.4. Structure de la demande
Actuellement, les seuils d’e´ligibilite´ par rapport au niveau de consommation annuelle sont les suivants:	au niveau fe´de´ral:	plus de 20 GWh
plus de 10 GWh a` partir du 31 décembre 2002; en Re´gion flamande:	plus de 1 GWh
plus de 56 Kva a` partir du 1er mars 2003	en Re´gion wallonne:	supe´rieur ou e´gal a` 20 GWh
supe´rieur ou e´gal a` 10 GWh pour le 31 décembre 2002. en Re´gion de Bruxelles-Capitale:   plus de 20 GWh
plus de 10 GWh a` partir du 01 janvier 2003. 6.5. Barrie`res a` l’entre´e
Selon les parties notifiantes, l’entre´e sur le marche´ est, en terme de couˆ ts, relativement facile puisqu’il suffit d’e´tablir un bureau d’achat/vente. En pratique, cela paraˆıt beaucoup moins e´vident. En effet, l’instruction du dossier et les auditions ont fait notamment apparaˆıtre l’existence de barrie`res juridiques et techniques a` l’entre´e sur le marche´ belge. 6.5.1. Barrie`res juridiques
6.5.1.1. Incertitudes juridiques
Force est de constater que la le´gislation, qui consacre en pratique le droit du client e´ligible a` se fournir aupre`s du fournisseur de son choix, est toujours incomple`te. Il manque toujours certaines re´glementations visant a` assurer un acce`s transparent et non discriminatoire au re´seau. Ce vide juridique a pour effet de favoriser de facto l’ope´rateur historique. 6.5.1.2. Dure´e des contrats de fourniture/Re´siliation
Un syste`me de transition a e´te´ mis en place en Re´gion wallonne pour les clients (devenant) e´ligibles. Selon ce syste`me, le gestionnaire du re´seau de distribution ne pouvant s’engager dans des activite´s de fourniture aux clients e´ligibles, de´signe un fournisseur a` cet effet (en l’occurrence Electrabel). L’intercommunale, deux mois avant la date d’e´ligibilite´, a l’obligation d’en informer le client final. Une fois devenu e´ligible, le client continue a` eˆtre approvisionne´ par le fournisseur de´signe´ par le gestionnaire, a` de´faut d’un accord passe´ avec un autre fournisseur. Il reste cependant libre de changer de fournisseur moyennant un pre´avis d’un mois. La liberte´ de changer de fournisseur et, partant, de mettre un terme a` l’approvisionnement par le fournisseur de´signe´ n’est totale qu’a` de´faut de contrat duˆ ment signe´ avec le fournisseur de´signe´. Il ressort de l’instruction et des auditions qu’un examen comple´mentaire s’ave`re ne´cessaire sur la dure´e de ces contrats. 6.5.2. Barrie`res techniques/physiques: interconnexion
L’importation d’e´lectricite´ de l’e´tranger est restreinte de manie`re substantielle par le manque de capacite´ des interconnexions aux frontie`res. M. de Garcia et M. Baeten et assiste´es par Me Vandencasteele, Me Brinckman et Me Vronincks, avocats a` Bruxelles; 1. les parties notifiantes

De´lais
La notification effectue´e le 25 avril 2002, e´tait incomple`te sur un point important au sens de l’article 5, § 2, de l’arreˆte´ royal du 23 mars 1993 relatif a` la notification des concentrations d’entreprises: elle ne contenait notamment pas l’accord constitutif de la concentration notifie´e, ni le proce`s-verbal d’Assemble´e ge´ne´rale du 25 mars 2002 portant modifications des statuts d’Interlux. Les socie´te´s ECS et Interlux sont des entreprises au sens de l’article 1er de la LPCE. Apre`s la concentration, ECS de´tiendra le controˆle exclusif de l’activite´ d’Interlux de fourniture d’e´lectricite´ aux clients e´ligibles (ou qui le deviendront). Sur la base des chiffres fournis par les parties dans la notification, les seuils des chiffres d’affaires vise´s a` l’article 11 de la loi sont atteints. 5. Marche´ concerne´
5.1. Secteur e´conomique concerne´
Le secteur e´conomique concerne´ par la concentration est celui de la production et de la distribution d’e´lectricite´ (code NACE: 40.1). 5.2. Marche´ de produits concerne´
Dans le secteur de l’e´lectricite´, cinq types d’activite´s diffe´rentes peuvent eˆtre distingue´s, soit la ge´ne´ration, le transport, la distribution, la fourniture et le ne´goce. —	La ge´ne´ration consiste en la production d’e´lectricite´. —	Le transport est l’acheminement de l’e´lectricite´ sur des caˆbles de haute tension. —	La distribution est l’acheminement de l’e´lectricite´ sur des caˆbles de moyenne et basse tension. —	La fourniture consiste en la livraison au consommateur final. —	Le ne´goce est l’achat et la revente d’e´lectricite´. Suite a` la libe´ralisation d’une partie du marche´ de l’e´lectricite´ initie´e par la directive CE 96/92, une distinction supple´mentaire doit eˆtre faite entre la fourniture d’e´lectricite´ aux clients e´ligibles et non e´ligibles (ou captifs,  
c.a`.d. qui ne peuvent pas choisir leur fournisseur). Ceux-ci rele`vent de deux marche´s de produits distincts, dans la mesure ou` les conditions de concurrence sont diffe´rentes, et ou` , le plus souvent, ils sont soumis a` des re´glementations spe´cifiques. C’est dans ce contexte que s’inscrit la pre´sente ope´ration puisque, en vertu de l’article 8, § 1er, du de´cret wallon, le gestionnaire du re´seau de distribution se voit interdire toute activite´ de fourniture aux clients e´ligibles. Ce gestionnaire du re´seau sera probablement l’intercommunale ou une nouvelle filiale de celle-ci cre´e´e a` cet effet. Electrabel est active directement ou indirectement sur les marche´s de production, de transport, de distribution, de fourniture d’e´lectricite´ et de ne´goce de produits lie´s a` l’e´lectricite´. Interlux est active sur les marche´s de la distribution et de la fourniture d’e´lectricite´. Cette dernie`re activite´, pour autant qu’elle concerne les clients devenant e´ligibles n’ayant pas choisi de fournisseur, sera exerce´e par ECS, filiale a` 100 % d’Electrabel. Par conse´quent, le marche´ de produits concerne´ est celui de la fourniture d’e´lectricite´ aux clients e´ligibles. 5.3. Marche´ ge´ographique concerne´
Le marche´ ge´ographique est au maximum national. En effet, compte tenu des proble`mes lie´s aux capacite´s limite´es des interconnexions, les importations sont restreintes dans une mesure assez significative. 6. Analyse concurrentielle
6.1. Structure de l’offre: position dominante d’Electrabel
Electrabel occupe une position privile´gie´e sur le marche´ belge puisqu’il de´tient des parts de marche´ extreˆmement e´leve´es quel que soit le marche´ envisage´. 6.1.1. Fourniture
Le marche´ de la fourniture d’e´lectricite´ aux clients e´ligibles en Belgique est estime´ par les parties en volume (GWh) a` 30.962,4 pour l’anne´e 2001. La part de marche´ d’Electrabel s’e´le`ve a` plus de 90 %. Aucun autre concurrent, quelle que soit sa puissance e´conomique et financie`re (EDF, RWE,  
E.ON), ne posse`de individuellement une part de marche´ supe´rieure ou e´gale a` 5 %. 6.1.2. Production
La position dominante d’Electrabel sur le marche´ de la fourniture aux clients e´ligibles doit e´galement eˆtre examine´e en tenant compte de la situation quasi monopolistique d’Electrabel sur le marche´ de la production en Belgique. Depuis 1995, la S.A. Electrabel et la S.A. SPE sont regroupe´es au sein d’une socie´te´ coope´rative (CPTE) dont le but est d’assurer la coordination de la production et du transport de l’e´nergie e´lectrique des deux entreprises.
